# rosettacommons/foundrysparkPowered by Gemini

# rosettacommons/foundrysparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 11, 2026Commit[`551a901`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/tree/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.Foundry provides a deep learning framework for designing protein and nucleic acid biomolecules\. It offers capabilities for model architecture, training, inference, and data processing tailored to biomolecular modeling\.

 The framework is organized around several key functional areas:

 - **Deep Learning Models for Biomolecular Design**: Foundry implements various deep learning models to address critical tasks in biomolecular engineering\. - **Sequence Design**: Models like ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN predict protein sequences given a fixed backbone structure, including specialized versions for protein\-ligand interactions\. See [Sequence Design Models \(MPNN\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#sequence-design-models-mpnn) for details\. - **All\-Atom Structure Prediction**: RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) predicts atomic coordinates and distograms for diverse biomolecules, including proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules, along with their interactions\. Refer to [All\-Atom Structure Prediction \(RF3\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3) for more information\. - **De Novo Interaction Design**: RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\) generates novel protein structures under specified constraints, enabling tasks such as designing protein binders and enzyme active sites\. Its extension, RFdiffusion3NA, expands these capabilities to multi\-polymer structures, including protein\-DNA\-RNA complexes\. More details are available in [De Novo Biomolecular Interaction Design \(RFdiffusion3\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-biomolecular-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3) and [De Novo Multi\-Polymer Interaction Design \(RFdiffusion3NA\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-multi-polymer-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3na)\.
- **Core Framework Infrastructure**: This layer provides general utilities for deep learning development, including package initialization, logging, type checking, and configuration management\. It integrates with Hydra for flexible configuration and dynamic resolution of modules and attributes, as described in [Hydra\-based Configuration and Dynamic Resolution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-hydra-based-configuration-and-dynamic-resolution)\.
- **Model Training and Inference**: A PyTorch Lightning Fabric\-based harness manages model training, validation, and checkpointing, supporting advanced techniques like distributed training and mixed precision\. This is further explained in [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\. A dedicated inference infrastructure separates model setup from execution, streamlining predictions\. See [Model Inference Infrastructure](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure) for details\.
- **Model Evaluation**: The framework includes a system for evaluating models, focusing on aggregating and computing multiple loss functions and metrics\. This system allows for custom metrics, dynamic input mapping, and conditional computation\. Refer to [Model Evaluation Metrics Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-evaluation-metrics-framework)\.
- **Extensible Callback System**: Foundry employs an extensible callback system that injects custom logic and monitoring into deep learning training and validation loops without altering core code\. This system facilitates model health monitoring, validation metric aggregation, and timing analysis\. More information is available in [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\.
- **CLI Utilities and Checkpoint Management**: Command\-line interface tools manage model checkpoints, facilitating installation, listing, and cleanup of pre\-trained models\. The system includes integrity verification for downloaded checkpoints\. See [Foundry CLI Utilities and Model Checkpoint Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#foundry-cli-utilities-and-model-checkpoint-management)\.
- **Testing and Deployment**: A comprehensive testing suite ensures correctness across numerical algorithms, neural network components, and hardware integrations\. An example Docker deployment demonstrates reproducible development environments and multi\-platform support\. This is elaborated in [Comprehensive Testing Suite](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#introduction-to-foundry-and-deep-learning-protein-design-comprehensive-testing-suite) and [Example Usage and Docker Deployment](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#introduction-to-foundry-and-deep-learning-protein-design-example-usage-and-docker-deployment)\.## Introduction to Foundry and Deep Learning Protein Design

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework is a platform for protein and nucleic acid design that leverages deep learning models\. It provides a comprehensive environment for model architecture, training, inference, and data processing, specifically tailored for biomolecular modeling\. The framework supports the entire lifecycle of deep learning model development, from initial setup to deployment and maintenance\.

 Foundry integrates several deep learning models that address various aspects of biomolecular design\. These include sequence design models such as ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN, which are utilized for inverse folding and designing sequences for given protein backbones\. For all\-atom structure prediction, the framework incorporates RosettaFold3 \(RF3\), capable of predicting atomic coordinates and distograms for diverse biomolecules\. Additionally, Foundry features *de novo* interaction design models like RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\) and its multi\-polymer extension, RFdiffusion3NA \(RFD3NA\), which enable the design of protein\-ligand and protein\-nucleic acid complexes under complex constraints\. More information on these specific models can be found in [Protein and Nucleic Acid Biomolecular Modeling Models](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models)\.

 The framework's core capabilities extend to managing global configurations, handling environment variables, and supporting multi\-platform deployments, including Docker\. Project management aspects are addressed through automated documentation generation using Sphinx, contribution guidelines, and standardized issue reporting via GitHub templates\. An example of Docker deployment is provided, illustrating a two\-stage build process for creating reproducible development environments and optional checkpoint downloads\. The robustness and correctness of the framework are ensured through a comprehensive pytest\-based testing suite that validates numerical algorithms, neural network components, data handling, and hardware\-specific features like Intel XPU support\. The overall infrastructure supports development and deployment workflows, ensuring consistency and reliability across different environments\.### Foundry's Core Framework and Development Infrastructure

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry provides a comprehensive framework for deep learning model development, supporting all stages from package initialization to multi\-platform deployment\. It establishes core configurations, manages global flags, and ensures robust development hygiene\.

 At initialization, the framework sets up environment variables and configures logging\. It includes conditional runtime type checking, which helps maintain code quality and detect errors early\. The system is designed to integrate with [pyproject\.toml L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L63) if available, and a global [\_\_init\_\_\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/__init__.py#L54) flag offers control over checkpointing behavior\.

 The framework incorporates various utilities to support its operations\. These include general\-purpose functions for runtime execution control, dictionary manipulation, and type enforcement, as detailed in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py)\. Constants, such as residue\-atom mappings, are defined in [`src/foundry/constants.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/constants.py) to standardize molecular modeling data\.

 For flexible configuration, Foundry integrates with Hydra\. Custom resolvers in [`src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py) enable dynamic importing of modules and attributes, allowing for adaptable system setups\. Additionally, these resolvers can convert [resolvers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py#L9) information into regular expressions, which is useful for filtering data based on chain properties\.

 To manage model checkpoints, Foundry provides command\-line utilities\. These tools allow users to install, list available, list installed, and clean up model checkpoints\. The system manages metadata for registered models, including descriptions and download paths, and resolves installation locations\. Checkpoint integrity is ensured through SHA256 hash verification during the download process\. Configuration of these CLI tools is dynamic, using environment variables and [\.env L2](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.env#L2) files\.

 Foundry also supports multi\-platform deployment, including Docker\. An example [`examples/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/docker/Dockerfile) illustrates a two\-stage build process for creating a custom Foundry Docker image, which can incorporate necessary dependencies and optionally download pre\-trained models\. This facilitates reproducible development and deployment environments\.

 For information on the extensible callback system, refer to [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\. Details on the Intel XPU integration can be found in [Intel XPU Integration for Accelerated Computing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-intel-xpu-integration-for-accelerated-computing)\.### Documentation and Project Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry's approach to project management includes structured documentation generation and standardized processes for community contributions\. Documentation is generated using Sphinx, with build automation managed by the [`docs/Makefile`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/Makefile)\. This Makefile orchestrates [Makefile L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/Makefile#L7) commands, allowing for flexible generation of various documentation formats, such as HTML\. Required Python packages for the documentation build, including [Makefile L1](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/Makefile#L1), [docs\_requirements\.txt L2](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/docs_requirements.txt#L2), [docs\_requirements\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/docs_requirements.txt#L3), and the [conf\.py L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/conf.py#L29) theme, are specified in [`docs/docs_requirements.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/docs_requirements.txt)\.

 The core configuration for the Sphinx documentation is found in [`docs/source/conf.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/conf.py)\. This file sets project\-specific metadata like name, copyright, and release version\. It also enables extensions for processing MyST Markdown files and adding copy buttons to code blocks\. The [conf\.py L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/conf.py#L29) HTML theme is customized through [conf\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/conf.py#L32) to incorporate Rosetta Commons branding colors and font styles, ensuring a consistent visual identity\. External JavaScript files, such as those for Google Analytics, are also integrated here, specifically [`docs/source/_static/ga.js`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/_static/ga.js)\. Troubleshooting information, particularly for common CUDA\-related installation issues, is provided in [`docs/source/installation_faq.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/source/installation_faq.md), offering guidance on compatible PyTorch ecosystem versions for NVIDIA GPUs\.

 For project hygiene and community interaction, Foundry utilizes GitHub issue templates located in [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE)\. These templates standardize the reporting of bugs via [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md), streamline feature requests through [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md), and guide users in asking questions or reporting unexpected outputs using [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/question-or-unexpected-outputs.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/question-or-unexpected-outputs.md)\. Each template automatically applies relevant labels and prompts for specific information, facilitating efficient triage and resolution by maintainers\.### Example Usage and Docker Deployment

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry provides practical examples of its application, particularly concerning Docker configurations for building custom Foundry Docker images\. These configurations facilitate the creation of reproducible development environments and allow for optional checkpoint downloads\.

 The Docker setup employs a two\-stage build process\. The initial [Dockerfile L15](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/docker/Dockerfile#L15) stage, defined in [`examples/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/docker/Dockerfile), establishes a comprehensive environment\. It starts from a base Ubuntu image, incorporates the [README\.md?plain=1 L26](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L26) package installer for efficient dependency management, and clones the Foundry source code\. Within this stage, a Python virtual environment is created, and Foundry, along with all its optional dependencies, is installed\. A key feature of this stage is the optional download of essential pre\-trained models \(checkpoints\), which are stored in a specified directory\.

 The final stage of the Docker build process begins with the same base image but focuses on creating a minimal runtime environment\. It selectively copies necessary artifacts, such as the installed Foundry application, the virtual environment, and any downloaded checkpoints, from the [Dockerfile L15](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/docker/Dockerfile#L15) stage\. This multi\-stage approach is designed to reduce the final image size by excluding build\-time dependencies\. The [make\.bat L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/docs/make.bat#L19) environment variable is then configured to ensure Foundry commands are directly accessible, and the working directory is set to the Foundry application root\. The default command for container startup is [README\.md?plain=1 L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L14), offering flexibility for users to execute various Foundry models and commands\.### Comprehensive Testing Suite

| Core Functionality | Test File | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rigid Body Alignment | test\_alignment\.py | Validates weighted\_rigid\_align for rigid transformations, float type support, masking, and weight exclusion\. |
| Architectural Blocks | test\_blocks\.py | Assesses FourierEmbedding \(output shape, value range\) and Dropout \(eval mode behavior, scaling, broadcast\_dim\) modules\. |
| Metric Aggregation | test\_callbacks\.py | Confirms StoreValidationMetricsInDFCallback accurately merges and de\-duplicates validation CSVs across ranks\. |
| Gradient Checkpointing | test\_checkpoint\.py | Ensures create\_custom\_forward binds kwargs and activation\_checkpointing preserves gradients and functionality\. |
| Checkpoint Registry | test\_checkpoint\_registry\.py | Verifies the logic for resolving checkpoint directories and environmental variable precedence\. |
| Common Utilities | test\_common\.py | Tests general utility functions like run\_once, exists, default, concat\_dicts, and listmap family\. |
| Component Parsing | test\_components\.py | Examines parsing of contig specifications, motif component extraction, and design pattern generation\. |
| Data Loading | test\_datasets\.py | Checks dataset and sampler instantiation, fallback mechanisms, and distributed data loader assembly\. |
| EMA Model Updates | test\_ema\.py | Validates the exponential moving average \(EMA\) update mechanism for model parameters and buffers\. |
| Rigid Body Transformations | test\_rigid\.py | Comprehensive testing of Rotation and Rigid classes for quaternion/matrix conversions, composition, and inversions\. |

The Foundry project employs a comprehensive test suite based on [pyproject\.toml L295](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L295) to validate its core functionalities\. This suite ensures the robustness and correctness of numerical algorithms, neural network components, data handling, checkpoint management, geometric transformations, and hardware\-specific features like XPU support\.

 Numerical algorithms, such as [alignment\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/alignment.py#L8) and [alignment\.py L87](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/alignment.py#L87), which are critical for SE\(3\) Kabsch alignment and RMSD calculation in structural prediction tasks, are thoroughly tested in [`tests/test_alignment.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_alignment.py)\. These tests confirm the accurate recovery of rigid transforms, proper handling of point exclusion via masks and weights, and output detachment across various input conditions and data types\.

 The behavior of fundamental neural network building blocks is verified in [`tests/test_blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_blocks.py)\. This includes testing the [blocks\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L7) layer for correct output shape and value range, and the [blocks\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L32) layer for its functionality in both evaluation and training modes, including scaling and broadcasting\. Further, the [EMA\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L9) \(Exponential Moving Average\) class, which maintains a shadow model for stable inference during training, has its update mechanisms, parameter handling, buffer copying, and operational modes validated in [`tests/test_ema.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_ema.py)\.

 Data handling and processing components are also covered\. For instance, [`tests/test_datasets.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_datasets.py) contains tests for functions responsible for building PyTorch [train\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L16) objects, verifying how datasets and samplers are initialized and wrapped, particularly in distributed training environments\. The conversion of contig specifications into structured data for models like RFdiffusion3 is tested in [`tests/test_components.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_components.py), ensuring correct parsing and robust error handling for various input formats\.

 Checkpoint management is a key aspect of Foundry, and its path resolution logic, including environment variable handling for checkpoint directories, is tested in [`tests/test_checkpoint_registry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_checkpoint_registry.py)\. This ensures that checkpoint files are correctly located and prioritized\. Additionally, the [fabric\.py L931](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L931) static method of the [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56), which identifies the most recent checkpoint, is tested in [`tests/test_fabric_trainer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_fabric_trainer.py) to verify its behavior under various directory conditions\. The command\-line interface for managing model checkpoints, including listing available and installed models, is tested in [`tests/test_download_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_download_checkpoints.py)\.

 Geometric transformations, specifically the [rigid\.py L278](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L278) and [rigid\.py L850](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L850) classes used for SE\(3\) frame primitives, are validated in [`tests/test_rigid.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_rigid.py)\. These tests cover constructors, application, inversion, composition, and conversions between different representations\. The [checkpoint\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/checkpoint.py#L38) utility, which aids in memory efficiency during training, is tested in [`tests/test_checkpoint.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_checkpoint.py) to ensure correct gradient propagation and output matching with non\-checkpointed execution\.

 Finally, hardware\-specific features, particularly the integration with Intel XPU devices for accelerated deep learning, are validated\. The custom accelerator, strategy, and precision plugins within PyTorch Lightning Fabric are tested in [`tests/test_xpu.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_xpu.py) to ensure efficient training and inference on Intel hardware\.

 The test suite also includes validation for the extensible callback system, as demonstrated by tests for [metrics\_logging\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/metrics_logging.py#L16) in [`tests/test_callbacks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_callbacks.py), which ensures correct merging and de\-duplication of validation metrics from distributed training runs\. General\-purpose utility functions are covered in [`tests/test_common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_common.py), verifying behavior for [all\.ipynb L102](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L102) values, once\-only execution, dictionary concatenation, list mapping, and [common\.py L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L106) dtype conversion\. Furthermore, the [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class for aggregating loss functions and the [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) for orchestrating multiple metrics are tested in [`tests/test_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_losses.py) and [`tests/test_metric.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/tests/test_metric.py) respectively, ensuring proper computation and management of evaluation criteria\.## Protein and Nucleic Acid Biomolecular Modeling Models

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework includes several deep learning models for protein and nucleic acid biomolecular modeling\. These models address tasks such as sequence design, all\-atom structure prediction, and *de novo* interaction design\.

 For sequence design, Foundry provides re\-implementations of ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN\. These models are designed to predict protein sequences given a fixed backbone structure, with specialized versions for handling ligand interactions and designing soluble membrane protein analogues\. Their core architecture relies on graph neural networks, which process protein structural information through graph embeddings and message passing mechanisms\. The framework supports comprehensive inference and training workflows, including data collation, specific loss functions like [nll\_loss\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7), and evaluation metrics such as sequence recovery and confidence scores\. Data pipelines are built to prepare structural data, incorporating various transformations for featurization and managing polymer\-ligand interfaces\. Details on the architectural components can be found in [MPNN Models: Core Architecture and Design Principles](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-mpnn-models-core-architecture-and-design-principles), and their training and inference workflows are described in [MPNN Models: Training and Inference Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-mpnn-models-training-and-inference-workflow)\.

 All\-atom structure prediction is addressed by RosettaFold3 \(RF3\)\. This model predicts atomic coordinates and distograms, integrating feature initializers, recyclers, and diffusion modules\. It is capable of handling diverse inputs, including arbitrary biomolecules, covalent modifications, and templating\. RF3 also includes confidence heads to predict metrics like pLDDT, PAE, and PDE, which can be used for early stopping during inference\. The model's data processing pipelines handle structural annotations, augmentations, and feature engineering for diffusion\-specific preprocessing\. For more information, refer to [RF3: All\-Atom Structure Prediction Architecture and Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rf3-all-atom-structure-prediction-architecture-and-mechanisms) and [RF3: Data Processing, Loss Functions, and Metrics for Structure Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rf3-data-processing-loss-functions-and-metrics-for-structure-prediction)\.

 For *de novo* biomolecular interaction design, Foundry offers RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\)\. This model uses a diffusion\-based approach to denoise atom coordinates and predict sequence information\. It coordinates token initialization and inference sampling for conditional generation, supporting various conditioning strategies such as motifs and buried/exposed residues\. Its data processing pipelines generate design reference features, featurize atoms, and integrate hydrogen bond information\. See [RFdiffusion3: Diffusion\-Based Interaction Design Architecture](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rfdiffusion3-diffusion-based-interaction-design-architecture) and [RFdiffusion3: Advanced Conditioning and Data Transformations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rfdiffusion3-advanced-conditioning-and-data-transformations) for further details\.

 An extension of RFdiffusion3, called RFdiffusion3NA, expands these capabilities to the *de novo* design of multi\-polymer structures, including protein\-DNA\-RNA complexes with atomic functional sites\. This model supports complex contig definitions and offers various conditioning options, such as sequence and sidechain constraints, and the integration of hydrogen bond information\. Its training and fine\-tuning frameworks are designed for distributed training and use specialized metrics to evaluate the design of these complex biomolecular assemblies\. Additional information can be found in [RFdiffusion3NA: Multi\-Polymer Design Capabilities and Conditioning](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rfdiffusion3na-multi-polymer-design-capabilities-and-conditioning) and [RFdiffusion3NA: Training and Evaluation for Multi\-Polymer Design](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-rfdiffusion3na-training-and-evaluation-for-multi-polymer-design)\.### MPNN Models: Core Architecture and Design Principles

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The core architecture for ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN models is primarily defined by the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class located in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py)\. This class orchestrates the process of protein sequence prediction using a graph neural network approach\. Its design incorporates graph featurization, structural context encoding, and sequence decoding mechanisms\.

 At a high level, the process begins with graph featurization, which transforms 3D protein coordinates and other structural data into node and edge features\. This is handled by a [mpnn\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L58), which can be specialized for different contexts such as membrane proteins \([graph\_embeddings\.py L791](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L791)\), proteins with Position\-Specific Scoring Matrices \([graph\_embeddings\.py L849](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L849)\), or protein\-ligand complexes \([graph\_embeddings\.py L897](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L897)\)\. These modules extract coordinates, compute distance and positional embeddings, and generate features that describe the local environment of each residue and the relationships between residues\. For instance, [graph\_embeddings\.py L897](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L897) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py) includes methods to gather and featurize nearest ligand atoms and side\-chain atoms, allowing the model to understand protein\-ligand interactions\.

 The featurized graph then undergoes encoding through a series of [mpnn\.py L136](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L136)\. These layers utilize message passing mechanisms to aggregate information across the graph, capturing complex structural context\. The message passing is implemented through [message\_passing\.py L114](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114) and [message\_passing\.py L227](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py), which update node and edge hidden states using multi\-layer perceptrons, GELU activations, Layer Normalization, and Dropout\.

 After encoding the structural context, the model proceeds to sequence prediction\. This involves decoding the residue sequences, which can be done either through a teacher\-forcing mechanism, where ground truth sequences guide the prediction, or an auto\-regressive approach, where residues are predicted iteratively\. The decoding process accounts for causality by establishing a decoding order and using causal masks to prevent information leakage\. Symmetry constraints can also be incorporated via [mpnn\.py L353](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L353) to ensure generated sequences adhere to structural symmetries\. The [mpnn\.py L872](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L872) method converts raw network outputs into sampled sequences by applying learned biases and temperature parameters, effectively guiding the amino acid choices\.

 For further details on the training and inference workflows for these models, refer to [MPNN Models: Training and Inference Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-mpnn-models-training-and-inference-workflow)\.### MPNN Models: Training and Inference Workflow

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides comprehensive workflows for both training and inference for ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN models\. The inference workflow is orchestrated by the [mpnn\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) found in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py)\. This engine loads pre\-trained models, validates configurations, and processes input data\. It utilizes a data transformation pipeline, built by [mpnn\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L61) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py), which prepares structural information for the model\. Input data is then fed through the model, and the engine decodes sequences\. During this process, metrics such as sequence recovery and confidence are computed using a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40), and the results are saved in formats like CIF and FASTA\. The engine supports various hardware platforms and ensures reproducibility through RNG seeding\. For more details on the core inference engine architecture, see [Core Inference Engine Architecture and Lifecycle](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-core-inference-engine-architecture-and-lifecycle)\.

 The training process for MPNN models is initiated by the [README\.md?plain=1 L124](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L124) script located in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py)\. This script manages the loading of training configurations, the preparation of data through a [train\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L9), and the sampling of data batches\. An important aspect of this is the batch sampling strategy, which uses [samplers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py#L9) from [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py)\. This sampler groups samples with similar token lengths to minimize padding, ensuring efficient use of computational resources\. Features for these batches are collated by [feature\_collator\.py L187](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py#L187), located in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py)\.

 The actual training is performed by the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) class in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py), which extends the [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56)\. This trainer manages the forward and backward passes, using [nll\_loss\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) from [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py) for calculating the loss\. Label smoothing in this context helps prevent model overconfidence and improves generalization\. Throughout training and validation, a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) is employed to track various performance indicators, including negative log\-likelihood \(NLL\) and sequence recovery\. For a deeper understanding of the overall training harness, refer to [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\. The [Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-metrics-and-loss-aggregation-framework) provides additional context on how metrics and losses are structured within Foundry\.### RF3: All\-Atom Structure Prediction Architecture and Mechanisms

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) model predicts all\-atom biomolecular structures by integrating diffusion\-based sampling, iterative refinement, and distogram prediction\. It handles diverse inputs, arbitrary biomolecules, covalent modifications, and templating, also providing confidence metrics\. The primary model, [RF3\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L56), predicts atomic coordinates and distograms, employing a feature initializer, a recycler for iterative refinement, a diffusion module for structure generation, and a distogram head for distance predictions\. The [RF3\.py L334](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L334) class extends this by incorporating a confidence head to predict metrics like pLDDT, PAE, and PDE, and supports early stopping during inference\.

 At its core, RF3's architecture is built upon several foundational components\. The [af3\_auxiliary\_heads\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py#L25) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py) is responsible for generating confidence scores\. The diffusion transformer architecture, detailed in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py), includes modules like [af3\_diffusion\_transformer\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py#L18) for atom\-level feature processing and [af3\_diffusion\_transformer\.py L283](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py#L283) for refining token\-level representations\. Attention mechanisms, such as [attention\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L18) and [attention\.py L157](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L157) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py), are used for updating pair representations\.

 The model also incorporates a Pairformer\-like architecture through layers defined in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py)\. These include [pairformer\_layers\.py L401](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L401) for setting up initial token and pairwise features, and [pairformer\_layers\.py L572](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L572) for refining Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) representations\. Outer product computations, defined in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/outer_product.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/outer_product.py), are used to aggregate MSA features for pair representation updates\. Structural bias features from 3D coordinates are generated by [structure\_bias\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/structure_bias.py#L7) and [structure\_bias\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/structure_bias.py#L25) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/structure_bias.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/structure_bias.py), using radial basis function \(RBF\) encoding\.

 The overall diffusion and recycling processes are orchestrated by modules in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py)\. The [RF3\_structure\.py L70](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70) handles noise removal from atomic coordinates, conditioned by [RF3\_structure\.py L174](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L174), while the [RF3\_structure\.py L257](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L257) iteratively refines sequence and pair representations, using [pairformer\_layers\.py L673](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L673) to incorporate template information\. The [RF3\_structure\.py L233](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L233) predicts inter\-residue distance distributions from learned pair features\.

 For more information on the RF3 model's data processing pipelines, refer to [RF3: Data Processing Pipelines for Diverse Inputs](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-data-processing-pipelines-for-diverse-inputs)\. Details on RF3's training and validation infrastructure can be found in [RF3: Training and Validation Infrastructure](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-training-and-validation-infrastructure)\. The inference engine and command\-line interface are described in [RF3: Inference Engine and CLI Usage](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-inference-engine-and-cli-usage)\.### RF3: Data Processing, Loss Functions, and Metrics for Structure Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) employs a sophisticated pipeline for handling biomolecular data, from initial structure preparation to feature generation, crucial for its all\-atom structure prediction capabilities\. The data processing starts by building a sequence of transforms using [pipelines\.py L129](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L129) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py)\. This pipeline cleans and prepares raw structural data, removing unnecessary components like hydrogens and handling incomplete or undesirable units\. It also annotates structures with identifiers and indices, ensuring that each atom and residue can be uniquely tracked throughout the process\.

 A key aspect of the data pipeline involves cropping and augmenting the data to enhance model robustness and generalize across diverse structural contexts\. This includes applying spatial and contiguous cropping, as well as random mirroring and centering for augmentation\. Feature generation is a comprehensive step, creating both token\-level and atom\-level features\. This involves loading and subsampling cached data, encoding features for various biomolecular components, and generating features from reference molecules\. It also includes identifying molecular automorphisms and mapping atoms to tokens\. Specialized RDKit\-based features are generated to capture chiral properties, and cyclic peptide bonds are detected and annotated to ensure accurate chemical representation\. Multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) are processed, including loading, pairing, merging, and encoding to provide evolutionary information to the model\.

 For diffusion\-based models like RF3, specific preprocessing steps are integrated\. This involves placing unresolved atoms, batching structures for noise sampling, and applying various forms of noise\. Ground truth conditioning, such as generating noised ground truth template distograms, helps guide the diffusion process\. The pipeline also includes specific transforms to generate features required for confidence prediction, such as atom frames and real atom indicators, which are then used by the confidence head of the model\. Error checking, such as [extra\_xforms\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/extra_xforms.py#L61) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/data/extra_xforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/extra_xforms.py), is integrated to ensure data integrity\.

 RF3 utilizes a suite of loss functions designed to optimize different aspects of structural accuracy and confidence\. The [af3\_confidence\_loss\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L18) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py) is crucial for evaluating the model's predicted confidence metrics, such as predicted Local Distance Difference Test \(pLDDT\), predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\), and predicted Distance Error \(PDE\)\. These are typically calculated as cross\-entropy losses between predicted logits and binned ground\-truth values\.

 For the core structural prediction, various losses are employed from [`models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py)\. These include [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) for minimizing the mean squared error between predicted and aligned ground\-truth coordinates, often incorporating a [af3\_losses\.py L544](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L544) for local accuracy\. [af3\_losses\.py L628](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L628) measures the accuracy of predicted distance distributions between residues\. [af3\_losses\.py L362](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L362) computes mean squared error for predicted intermolecular bond distances\. Additionally, [af3\_losses\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L10) and [af3\_losses\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L56) align predicted structures with ground truth by resolving symmetries at the residue and subunit levels\. For chirality, [loss\.py L136](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py#L136) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py) computes specialized gradients for chiral centers to ensure stereochemical correctness\.

 The model's performance is comprehensively evaluated using a range of metrics, many of which are implemented as [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) subclasses to integrate into a larger evaluation framework\. For accuracy, [lddt\.py L205](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L205) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py) provides an overall measure of local structural similarity, while [lddt\.py L268](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L268) and [lddt\.py L371](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L371) offer more granular assessments of interface and intra\-chain accuracy, respectively\. Chiral accuracy is measured by [chiral\.py L158](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L158) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py), which quantifies errors related to the stereochemistry of molecules\.

 Beyond direct structural comparisons, metrics also assess global qualities and errors\. [clashing\_chains\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py#L10) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py) identifies undesirable steric clashes between chains\. [distogram\.py L178](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L178) and [distogram\.py L317](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L317) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py) evaluate the quality of predicted distance distributions\. The predicted confidence scores are themselves evaluated by [predicted\_error\.py L43](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L43) and [predicted\_error\.py L73](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L73) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py), which estimate the predicted TM\-score and interface TM\-score from the model's predicted aligned error \(PAE\)\. [rasa\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/rasa.py#L9) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/rasa.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/rasa.py) quantifies the solvent accessibility of unresolved regions, providing insights into structural compactness and potential disorder\. Utility functions in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/metric_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/metric_utils.py) support these metrics by handling binning, masking, and statistical aggregation\.### RFdiffusion3: Diffusion\-Based Interaction Design Architecture

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\) utilizes a diffusion\-based approach for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design\. The core of the model, defined by the [RFD3\.py L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py#L19) class in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py), acts as a high\-level orchestrator for the different components involved in both training and inference\. This class coordinates the [encoders\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36), the central [RF3\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L71), and the [engine\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) to perform conditional generation and classifier\-free guidance, enabling the model to generate novel protein structures under specified constraints\.

 The central component for denoising and sequence prediction is the [RFD3\_diffusion\_module\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32), located in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py)\. This module processes noisy atom coordinates and various structural and sequence features\. It employs several sub\-modules, including a [blocks\.py L439](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L439) for sequence prediction, a [blocks\.py L638](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L638) and [blocks\.py L585](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L585) for processing local atomic and token features, and a [blocks\.py L710](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L710) to integrate information\. The module's [EMA\.py L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L63) method manages the diffusion step, while [RFD3\_diffusion\_module\.py L267](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L267) handles iterative refinement\. Position scaling is also managed to adjust atom coordinates based on noise levels\.

 Token initialization, handled by the [encoders\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py), sets up initial single and pairwise representations for the biomolecules\. This involves embedding one\-dimensional features, downcasting atom features, and incorporating positional and motif embeddings to create a rich initial representation\.

 The inference process is governed by the [inference\_sampler\.py L572](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L572) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py)\. This class is responsible for orchestrating the iterative denoising process during the generative phase\. It handles specific sampling configurations, including [inference\_sampler\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L58) for designs involving fixed structural motifs and [inference\_sampler\.py L363](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L363) for designs requiring symmetric structures\. This sampler applies noise, performs denoising steps using the [RF3\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L71), and can incorporate Classifier\-Free Guidance \(CFG\) to enhance sample quality\. The [inference\_sampler\.py L376](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L376) function within [inference\_sampler\.py L363](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L363) ensures that generated structures adhere to specified symmetry during the diffusion process\. Utility functions for Classifier\-Free Guidance, such as [cfg\_utils\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py#L4) and [cfg\_utils\.py L70](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py#L70) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py), modify conditioning features and atom coordinates to control the generation process\.

 The neural network layers, found in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers), comprise fundamental building blocks for processing hierarchical data\. These include various attention mechanisms like [attention\.py L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/attention.py#L91) and [attention\.py L188](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/attention.py#L188) for efficient information exchange between different parts of the biomolecule\. Memory\-optimized [chunked\_pairwise\.py L17](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py#L17) and [chunked\_pairwise\.py L142](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py#L142) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py) manage pairwise feature computations for large structures, optimizing memory usage\. Data utility functions in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/block_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/block_utils.py) assist in mask generation, atom grouping, and attention index creation\. Architectural blocks like [blocks\.py L659](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L659) and [blocks\.py L585](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L585) \(in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py)\) facilitate the transformation and transfer of information between sequence and atomic representations\. Normalization layers such as [layer\_utils\.py L27](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/layer_utils.py#L27) and adaptive conditioning modules like [layer\_utils\.py L64](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/layer_utils.py#L64) \(in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/layer_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/layer_utils.py)\) contribute to model stability and flexibility\.### RFdiffusion3: Advanced Conditioning and Data Transformations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RFdiffusion3 employs advanced data processing and transformation pipelines to prepare biomolecular data for design tasks, particularly focusing on how conditioning information influences generative models\. These pipelines convert raw structural data into a format suitable for deep learning, incorporating methods for creating design reference features, featurizing atoms, handling symmetry, and integrating hydrogen bond information\.

 Central to this process are conditioning strategies, which guide the model towards desired design outcomes\. These strategies are managed through various components within the [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms) directory\. The module [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py) defines the foundational logic for managing these conditions, including how motif features are extracted and default annotations are applied\. For instance, [conditioning\_base\.py L55](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L55) extracts properties of predefined motifs, while [conditioning\_base\.py L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L69) ensures basic structural information is consistently available\.

 Specific training conditions, such as [training\_conditions\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) and [training\_conditions\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py), enable diverse design scenarios\. [training\_conditions\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) allows for the definition of "islands" of residues as motifs, with options to diffuse sidechains, sample subgraphs, or fix sequence and coordinates, providing flexibility in controlling the design space\. [training\_conditions\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) is tailored for protein\-protein interaction design, where one protein might be designated as a fixed motif\. These conditions utilize utilities like [conditioning\_utils\.py L15](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py#L15) and [conditioning\_utils\.py L87](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py#L87) from [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py) to generate masks that guide the model during training\. The [conditioning\_base\.py L315](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) transformation in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py) manages the expansion of "unindexed" motif tokens and generates attention masks, preventing information leakage during generation\.

 Featurization is another critical aspect\. The [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py) module, includes transformations such as [design\_transforms\.py L117](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L117), which generates atom\-level reference positions and masks, and [design\_transforms\.py L346](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L346), which adds features like binned relative solvent accessibility \(RASA\) and active hydrogen bond donor/acceptor flags\. [design\_transforms\.py L399](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L399) annotates atoms with their structural roles \(e\.g\., backbone, sidechain, virtual\), and motif\-specific flags\. The [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py) module contains [rasa\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py#L7) to compute and store solvent accessibility\.

 Hydrogen bond information, crucial for biomolecular interactions, is incorporated using modules like [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py) and [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py)\. These modules can add explicit hydrogen atoms and calculate hydrogen bonds using either [hbonds\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py#L4) and [scoring\.py L98](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/scoring.py#L98) or the external [README\.md?plain=1 L143](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L143) program, annotating the structures with active donor and acceptor sites\.

 Symmetry handling is managed by [symmetry\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L10) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py), which adds symmetry\-related features and transformation matrices to the data, facilitating the design of symmetric biomolecular assemblies\. This works in conjunction with the symmetry utilities detailed in [RFdiffusion3: Inference Engine and Input Specification](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-biomolecular-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3-rfdiffusion3-inference-engine-and-input-specification)\.

 Data augmentation and diffusion\-specific preprocessing are also part of these pipelines\. [design\_transforms\.py L531](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L531) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py) applies random rigid body perturbations to motifs, enhancing the model's robustness\. For diffusion models, coordinates can be augmented with noise, with options to zero out noise for fixed motif atoms\. The [virtual\_atoms\.py L139](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/virtual_atoms.py#L139) transformation in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/virtual_atoms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/virtual_atoms.py) ensures consistent input dimensions by padding residues with virtual atoms\.

 The construction of these comprehensive data processing pipelines is orchestrated by functions like [pipelines\.py L311](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py#L311) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py)\. This function dynamically includes various transformations based on the inference status, specific conditioning requirements, and configuration parameters, ensuring that the data is appropriately preprocessed for the intended design task\. These pipelines integrate preprocessing steps, cropping \(e\.g\., [pipelines\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L62), [ppi\_transforms\.py L307](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/ppi_transforms.py#L307)\), feature generation, and diffusion\-specific transforms \([pipelines\.py L66](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L66)\), utilizing route mechanisms \([pipelines\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L115), [pipelines\.py L122](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L122)\) for conditional application of transformations\.### RFdiffusion3NA: Multi\-Polymer Design Capabilities and Conditioning

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RFdiffusion3NA is an expanded version of RFdiffusion3 that facilitates the *de novo* design of multi\-polymer structures, including protein, DNA, and RNA complexes, with the ability to define atomic functional sites\. This model supports sophisticated conditioning tasks to precisely control design constraints during both training and inference\.

 The model handles multi\-polymer contig definitions, allowing users to specify RNA \([README\.md?plain=1 L161](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L161)\) or DNA \([README\.md?plain=1 L392](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L392)\) suffixes in contig strings \(e\.g\., [README\.md?plain=1 L55](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/README.md?plain=1#L55)\) to define multi\-polymer chains\. This enables complex designs combining different biomolecule types\. Input specifications, similar to RFdiffusion3, use JSON/YAML files for design constraints, with added support for nucleic acid types\.

 RFdiffusion3NA offers various conditioning options, including fixing the sequence, unfixing the sequence for inverse folding \(akin to MPNN\), or unfixing only sidechains \(similar to PLACER/ChemNet\-style design\)\.
