It integrates hydrogen bond conditioning during design, requiring the external [README\.md?plain=1 L143](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L143) program\.

 The data processing pipelines for RFdiffusion3NA, found in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms), are crucial for preparing structural data\. These pipelines handle filtering, cropping, featurization, and augmentation\. Key transformations include assigning molecular types \(protein, RNA, DNA, ligand\) via [util\_transforms\.py L87](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py#L87) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/util_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/util_transforms.py) and generating token\-level features through [util\_transforms\.py L366](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py#L366) in the same file\. Atomic\-level features are added using [design\_transforms\.py L399](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L399) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py)\.

 Conditioning for generative tasks is managed through base transform classes in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py), such as [conditioning\_base\.py L213](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L213) for selecting strategies and [conditioning\_base\.py L315](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) for dynamically expanding "unindexed" motifs \(tokens to be generated or diffused\)\. This allows for relative position encoding\. Specific training conditions, such as [training\_conditions\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) for selecting contiguous segments as motifs and [training\_conditions\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) for protein\-protein interaction training, are implemented in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py)\.

 Further featurization includes generating reference features for design, similar to AlphaFold3, via [design\_transforms\.py L117](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L117) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py), and atom\-wise features like RASA \(Relative Accessible Surface Area\) calculated by [rasa\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py#L7) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/rasa.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/rasa.py)\. Hydrogen bond information can be calculated using [hbonds\.py L225](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py#L225) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds.py) or by integrating with the [README\.md?plain=1 L143](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L143) program via [hbonds\_hbplus\.py L177](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py#L177) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py)\. For nucleic acids, [na\_geom\.py L103](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom.py#L103) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom.py) generates 2D token\-token matrices representing secondary structure from base\-pair annotations or user specifications\. Symmetry\-related features are also integrated through [symmetry\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L10) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/symmetry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/symmetry.py)\.

 The model supports advanced conditioning and transformations, including defining secondary structure \(SS\) conditioning and base\-pair constraints in its input specification, as highlighted in the documentation found in [`models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md)\. This allows for precise control over the design of nucleic acid structures\. Ligand\-conditioned aptamer design is also possible, leveraging features like [input\_parsing\.py L170](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170), [input\_parsing\.py L174](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174), and [input\_parsing\.py L191](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/input_parsing.py#L191) to guide the generation process\. Hybrid RNA\-protein designs utilize [input\_parsing\.py L135](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L135) to remove residues from positional indexing and [input\_parsing\.py L152](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152) to preserve specific structural elements\.

 The inference engine, specifically [engine\.py L139](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L139) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/engine.py), manages the orchestration of the inference workflow, processing complex multi\-polymer input specifications, handling atom selection and canonicalization, and facilitating the distributed loading of design data\. This ensures efficient generation of protein\-DNA\-RNA complexes\. The [inference\_sampler\.py L572](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L572) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/model/inference_sampler.py) is central to this process, handling motif\-guided and symmetry\-aware variations during diffusion sampling\. See [RFdiffusion3NA: Advanced Input Specification and Inference Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-multi-polymer-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3na-rfdiffusion3na-advanced-input-specification-and-inference-workflow) for further details on input specification and inference\.### RFdiffusion3NA: Training and Evaluation for Multi\-Polymer Design

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RFdiffusion3NA model utilizes a comprehensive framework for training and fine\-tuning to enable the *de novo* design of multi\-polymer structures\. The primary training script, [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/train.py), orchestrates the entire process, leveraging [README\.md?plain=1 L150](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L150) for distributed training across multiple GPUs and nodes\. This setup ensures efficient processing of large datasets and model scales\.

 Training involves configuring datasets, which can draw from PDB and CCD mirrors, and is flexible enough to integrate custom datasets compatible with AtomWorks\. During training, the model generates various "problems" with diverse conditioning tasks, defined through configuration files\. This approach allows the model to learn robust design principles under different constraints\. Logging mechanisms, including a [pyproject\.toml L30](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L30) logger or a [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L81) logger, track training progress and metrics\.

 Model training and validation are managed by the [rfd3\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33), found in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/rfd3na.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/rfd3na.py), which extends the [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) defined in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/fabric_trainer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/fabric_trainer.py)\. This trainer handles the core training loop, validation steps, and checkpointing, including loading from previous checkpoints and managing model state\. A key aspect is its ability to process unindexed structural tokens, allowing for flexible insertion and modification of molecular components during design\.

 Evaluation of [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L81) designs relies on a suite of specialized metrics, detailed in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics)\. These metrics assess various aspects of the designed protein\-DNA\-RNA complexes, including clash detection, chain break analysis, sequence recovery, hydrogen bond analysis, and nucleic acid secondary structure similarity\. For instance, the [losses\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L7) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics/losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics/losses.py) calculates cross\-entropy on token sequences, while the [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) computes a weighted mean squared error \(MSE\) between predicted and ground truth coordinates, incorporating a smoothed Local Distance Difference Test \(LDDT\) loss for structural similarity\. The [dump\_validation\_structures\.py L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py#L19) in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py) automatically saves predicted structures and trajectories during validation, enabling detailed post\-analysis\. These metrics are crucial for ensuring the quality and biological relevance of the generated multi\-polymer designs\.## Core Framework Development

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides the core infrastructure for deep learning model development, training, evaluation, and inference, with a specific focus on molecular modeling applications\. It manages fundamental aspects such as package initialization, logging, type checking, global flag management, and integration with GPU hardware\. An extensible callback system allows for injecting custom logic at various stages of the deep learning pipeline\.

 The framework is initialized by loading environment variables from [\.env L2](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.env#L2) files, which configure settings such as debug mode, type checking, and NaN checking\. A package\-specific logger is established, and runtime type checking can be conditionally enabled\. Foundry also attempts to integrate with [README\.md?plain=1 L39](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L39) if available and not explicitly disabled, setting relevant environment variables for its configuration\. A global flag, [\_\_init\_\_\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/__init__.py#L54), controls checkpointing behavior across the package\. These initialization and configuration steps are handled in [`src/foundry/__init__.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/__init__.py)\.

 Foundry includes a comprehensive suite of general\-purpose utility functions in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py) that support common programming tasks like ensuring a function runs only once, checking for null values, concatenating dictionaries, and mapping functions over lists\. Additionally, a set of constants, such as [constants\.py L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/constants.py#L3) in [`src/foundry/constants.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/constants.py), provides mappings crucial for defining protein structural properties\.

 The framework integrates with Hydra for configuration management, particularly through custom resolvers defined in [`src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py)\. These resolvers enable dynamic importing of modules and attributes within Hydra configurations and convert [resolvers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py#L9) or [resolvers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py#L9) enum attributes into regular expressions, which can be used for flexible data filtering\.

 Foundry's evaluation metrics framework, detailed in [`src/foundry/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics), offers a modular approach to assessing model performance\. It includes an abstract [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) class, a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) for orchestrating multiple metrics with flexible input mapping and tag\-based conditional computation, and a [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class for aggregating various loss functions\.

 The neural network building blocks in [`src/foundry/model`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model) provide reusable layers for constructing model architectures\. This includes a [blocks\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L7) layer for generating Fourier features and a [blocks\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L32) layer that supports broadcasting across a specified dimension\.

 An extensible callback system, located in [`src/foundry/callbacks`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks), allows developers to monitor and log various aspects of the training and validation processes\. The [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) abstract class in [`src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py) defines hooks that are invoked at different stages of the training loop\. Specific callback implementations track model health by monitoring gradients, weights, and activations, aggregate and persist validation metrics to CSV files, analyze the timing of training and validation stages, and log diverse training\-related information such as model parameters, dataset sampling ratios, and learning rates\. This system leverages [ddp\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L5) for distributed training environments and [ddp\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L58) for controlled message output\. For further details on the callback system, refer to [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\.### Core Framework Initialization and Configuration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry package's initialization process establishes its operational environment, managing configurations, and activating core functionalities\. At its foundation, the system loads environment variables using an [\_\_init\_\_\.py L6](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/__init__.py#L6) instance, which dictates behaviors such as debug mode, runtime type checking, and NaN checking\. This approach allows for flexible configuration without modifying the codebase directly, adapting to different deployment or development needs\.

 A key aspect of initialization is the conditional activation of runtime type checking\. If configured, the [pyproject\.toml L95](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L95) package integrates with [pyproject\.toml L34](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L34) to enforce type validation across its modules, enhancing code robustness\. Similarly, the framework attempts to integrate with [README\.md?plain=1 L39](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L39) if a CUDA\-enabled GPU is detected and not explicitly disabled\. This integration provides support for specialized hardware acceleration, particularly for equivariant neural networks\. The availability of [README\.md?plain=1 L39](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L39) is tracked by a global flag, allowing other parts of the system to adapt their behavior accordingly\.

 Additionally, the initialization process manages global flags that control fundamental system behaviors, such as [\_\_init\_\_\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/__init__.py#L54)\. This flag determines whether checkpointing operations, crucial for saving model states during training, should be active, offering control over resource usage and data persistence\. These initial setup steps are primarily orchestrated within the [pyproject\.toml L95](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L95) package's [ddp\.py L90](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L90) file\. Further details on how model checkpoints are managed and accessed can be found in [Foundry CLI Utilities and Model Checkpoint Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#foundry-cli-utilities-and-model-checkpoint-management) and [Checkpoint Management and Registry](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-checkpoint-management-and-registry)\.### Advanced Utilities and Common Functions

```
@run_once
def initialize_system():
    """A function that should only run once, e.g., for setup."""
    print("System initialized!")
    # ... potentially complex setup logic ...

def get_config_value(key: str, default_value: Any) -> Any:
    """Retrieves a configuration value, using 'default' for fallbacks."""
    config = {"database_url": "postgres://user:pass@host:port/db"} # Stub: In reality, this would load from a file or env
    return default(config.get(key), default_value)

# First call executes the function
initialize_system()
# Subsequent calls do nothing
initialize_system()

print(f"Database URL: {get_config_value('database_url', 'sqlite:///data.db')}")
print(f"API Key: {get_config_value('api_key', 'default_api_key_123')}")
```

The Foundry framework leverages a suite of general\-purpose utility functions and constants to streamline development and enhance code readability and robustness\. These utilities address common programming patterns, dictionary manipulation, type enforcement, and provide fundamental molecular modeling constants\.

 To control runtime execution and prevent redundant operations, the [common\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L8) decorator, defined in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py), ensures that a decorated function executes only once per process\. This is particularly useful for initialization routines or resource\-intensive setups that should not be repeated\. Additionally, null and existence checks are simplified through functions like [common\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L33), [common\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L38), [common\.py L43](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L43), and [common\.py L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L48) in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py), providing concise ways to handle optional values and logical conditions\.

 For data structures, [common\.py L53](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L53) in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py) allows for combining multiple dictionaries that share common keys, aggregating their values into lists\. Iteration and transformation of lists are facilitated by [common\.py L66](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L66) and [common\.py L84](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L84) in the same file, which apply a function to each element, optionally including its index, and return a new list\.

 Type enforcement for PyTorch tensors is managed by [common\.py L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L106) in [`src/foundry/common.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py), which ensures a tensor adheres to a specified data type, preventing unnecessary conversions if the type already matches\.

 A crucial constant for structural definition in molecular modeling is [constants\.py L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/constants.py#L3), located in [`src/foundry/constants.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/constants.py)\. This dictionary maps various residue types to specific "TIP" atoms, which are typically critical for maintaining structural integrity or acting as fixed reference points during computational operations\.

 Further utilities supporting the overall framework are elaborated in [Comprehensive Utility Suite for Molecular Modeling](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-comprehensive-utility-suite-for-molecular-modeling), while the core package initialization, which integrates some of these utilities, is detailed in [Core Framework Initialization and Configuration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-core-framework-initialization-and-configuration)\.### Hydra\-based Configuration and Dynamic Resolution

```
model:
  _target_: ${resolve_import:foundry.models.custom_model_module, MyCustomModel} # Dynamically import a model class
  # ... other model parameters
optimizer:
  _target_: ${resolve_import:torch.optim, AdamW} # Import an optimizer from a common library
  lr: 0.001

data_filter:
  protein_chains: ${chain_type_info_to_regex:PROTEINS} # Resolve to a regex matching all protein ChainTypes
  specific_chains: ${chain_type_info_to_regex:ALPHA_HELIX, BETA_SHEET} # Resolve multiple ChainTypeInfo enums
  single_chain_type: ${chain_type_info_to_regex:DNA} # Resolve a single ChainType
```

Foundry integrates with Hydra to provide a flexible and dynamic configuration system for its deep learning models\. This integration is managed through custom resolvers defined in [`src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py)\. One key resolver enables dynamic importing of modules and attributes directly within Hydra configuration files\. This allows referencing classes, functions, or variables without hardcoding them, supporting modularity and reusability across different model configurations\. For instance, a model's architecture or a specific optimizer can be specified as a string in a YAML file, and Hydra will dynamically load it at runtime\.

 Additionally, Foundry utilizes a custom Hydra resolver to convert [resolvers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py#L9) or [resolvers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/hydra/resolvers.py#L9) enum attributes into regular expression strings\. This functionality is particularly useful for filtering data based on protein chain types, offering a powerful mechanism for flexible data selection and processing within diverse biomolecular modeling tasks\. By defining these resolvers, Foundry enhances its ability to manage complex configurations for various deep learning applications in protein and nucleic acid design\.### Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry's modular framework facilitates the definition and management of evaluation metrics and loss functions\. The [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) orchestrates the computation of various metrics, allowing for flexible input mapping and conditional execution based on tags\. Individual metrics are defined by inheriting from the abstract [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) class, which mandates the implementation of a [metric\.py L319](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L319) method for the actual calculation\. This design supports extracting necessary arguments from diverse input structures and applying tag\-based filtering for selective metric computation\.

 For aggregating loss functions, the [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class, inheriting from [weights\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20), enables the combination of multiple individual loss computations\. It instantiates various loss functions from configurations and, during its forward pass, sums their scalar outputs while merging detailed loss values into a single dictionary\. This approach ensures that both a total loss value and granular insights into individual loss contributions are available, supporting the detailed analysis of model training performance\.### Training Utilities for Stability and Efficiency

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides advanced utilities to enhance the stability and efficiency of deep learning model training\. These include mechanisms for stabilizing model performance through Exponential Moving Average \(EMA\), conserving memory during training with gradient checkpointing, and dynamically adjusting learning rates with custom schedulers\.

 One such utility is the Exponential Moving Average \(EMA\), implemented in the [EMA\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L9) class in [`src/foundry/training/EMA.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py)\. This mechanism maintains a [EMA\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L10) copy of the model's weights, which are updated as an exponential moving average of the active model's weights\. During evaluation, predictions are made using this [EMA\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L10) model rather than the primary training model\. This approach helps to smooth out weight fluctuations during training, often leading to more robust and generalized models\.

 To address memory constraints, particularly with large models, Foundry integrates gradient checkpointing utilities\. The [checkpoint\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/checkpoint.py#L38) decorator in [`src/foundry/training/checkpoint.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/checkpoint.py) selectively applies [mpnn\.py L320](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L320) during the forward pass when gradients are enabled\. This technique recomputes intermediate activations during the backward pass rather than storing them, significantly reducing memory usage at the cost of a slight increase in computation time\. The utility also handles keyword arguments for checkpointed functions by creating a custom forward pass, ensuring compatibility with PyTorch's checkpointing API\.

 For flexible optimization strategies, Foundry includes a custom learning rate scheduler, [schedulers\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/schedulers.py#L7), defined in [`src/foundry/training/schedulers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/schedulers.py)\. This scheduler implements a two\-phase approach: a linear warmup phase followed by a decay phase where the learning rate gradually decreases\. The [schedulers\.py L66](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/schedulers.py#L66) dataclass provides a structured way to configure these schedulers, allowing for customization of parameters like the warmup steps, decay factor, and frequency of updates, aligning with common practices in PyTorch Lightning for managing optimizer schedules\.### Comprehensive Utility Suite for Molecular Modeling

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry provides a comprehensive suite of utilities designed to support various aspects of deep learning molecular modeling, encompassing geometric transformations, data management, configuration, logging, and PyTorch\-specific operations, including specialized support for Intel XPU hardware\.

 For handling 3D rigid body transformations, the framework includes utilities for weighted rigid body alignment and RMSD calculation, which are fundamental for comparing and superimposing molecular structures\. Classes like [rigid\.py L278](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L278) and [rigid\.py L850](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L850) in [`src/foundry/utils/rigid.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py) are designed to manage 3D rotations and combined rigid transformations \(rotation and translation\) in a [README\.md?plain=1 L22](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L22)\-compatible and differentiable manner\. These classes provide methods for representation conversion \(e\.g\., between rotation matrices and quaternions\), composition of transformations, and application to 3D points\. Furthermore, utilities for rotation and translation augmentation in [`src/foundry/utils/rotation_augmentation.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/rotation_augmentation.py) enable robust training by introducing variability in 3D coordinate data\.

 The framework also offers utilities for parsing and validating protein component strings, generating atom masks, and handling contig specifications in [`src/foundry/utils/components.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/components.py)\. This functionality is critical for defining and manipulating specific regions of proteins and nucleic acids in molecular design tasks\.

 Efficient data loading and management are facilitated through utilities in [`src/foundry/utils/datasets.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/datasets.py), which support dataset and sampler instantiation, composition, and distributed [train\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L16) assembly with fallback mechanisms\. This allows for resilient and scalable data pipelines, particularly important in large\-scale deep learning experiments\. Additionally, the [squashfs\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/squashfs.py#L18) in [`src/foundry/utils/squashfs.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/squashfs.py) acts as a singleton for lazy, thread\-safe mounting and automatic cleanup of [squashfs\.py L51](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/squashfs.py#L51) files, optimizing access to read\-only compressed archives\.

 Configuration and logging are streamlined with functions in [`src/foundry/utils/logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/logging.py), which manage warning suppression, structured configuration display, and detailed logging using [pyproject\.toml L31](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L31) for enhanced console output\. This is complemented by instantiator utilities in [`src/foundry/utils/instantiators.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/instantiators.py) that dynamically create objects like callbacks and loggers from [ddp\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L7) configurations\. The distributed data parallel \(DDP\) utilities in [`src/foundry/utils/ddp.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py) further enhance logging by providing rank\-aware loggers and enabling dynamic accelerator configuration based on available hardware, which is especially relevant for [Distributed Training and Hardware Acceleration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness-distributed-training-and-hardware-acceleration)\.

 PyTorch\-specific operations are consolidated in [`src/foundry/utils/torch.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/torch.py), providing utilities for tensor manipulation, shape assertions, NaN checks, scatter\-mean aggregation, and performance timing\. This includes conditional checks for numerical stability and a flexible timing system for profiling\. A notable feature is the integration of Intel XPU support within [`src/foundry/utils/xpu`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu), enabling efficient training and inference on Intel hardware through custom PyTorch Lightning Fabric components like [xpu\_accelerator\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_accelerator.py#L9) and [single\_xpu\_strategy\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/single_xpu_strategy.py#L13)\. This allows for broad hardware compatibility within the Foundry framework\. Model checkpoint management is also supported through utilities for loading weights from checkpoints and applying parameter freezing policies as detailed in [`src/foundry/utils/weights.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/weights.py)\.### Intel XPU Integration for Accelerated Computing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry integrates with Intel XPU devices to accelerate deep learning operations by providing specialized components within PyTorch Lightning Fabric\. This integration is crucial for efficiently training and inferring models on Intel hardware\.

 Central to this integration is the [xpu\_accelerator\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_accelerator.py#L9) class, defined in [`src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_accelerator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_accelerator.py), which acts as an interface between Lightning Fabric and Intel XPU devices\. It manages device setup, parsing of device specifications, and reporting available XPU devices, similar to how other accelerators manage GPU resources\.

 For single\-device operations, the [single\_xpu\_strategy\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/single_xpu_strategy.py#L13) in [`src/foundry/utils/xpu/single_xpu_strategy.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/single_xpu_strategy.py) is employed\. This strategy ensures that training and inference workflows are correctly orchestrated on a single XPU, performing a runtime check for XPU availability to prevent execution on unsupported systems\.

 Mixed precision training on Intel XPU devices is handled by the [xpu\_precision\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_precision.py#L11) class, found in [`src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_precision.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_precision.py)\. This component extends Lightning Fabric's mixed precision capabilities to XPU, enabling automatic type casting for [xpu\_precision\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_precision.py#L25) or [README\.md?plain=1 L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L40) operations during the forward pass, thereby improving performance and memory efficiency\.

 These components are exposed through the [`src/foundry/utils/xpu/__init__.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/__init__.py) entry point and are automatically utilized by the [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) when XPU is detected\. This allows for seamless adoption of Intel XPU devices for accelerating deep learning workloads within the Foundry framework\. For a deeper understanding of the core training mechanisms that utilize these components, refer to [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\.## Sequence Design Models \(MPNN\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section describes the re\-implementation of ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN within the Foundry framework for protein sequence design\. These models enable sequence design given a fixed backbone structure, extend to include ligands \(small molecules, ions, DNA/RNA\), and support the design of soluble and functional membrane protein analogues\. The Foundry implementation supports both inference and training capabilities, encompassing graph featurization, sequence prediction, data collation, loss computation, and model architecture\. The core logic for these models resides in the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class within [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py), which is a [weights\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20) central to protein sequence prediction\.

 The framework provides specific tools for graph featurization, located in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py)\. These include [graph\_embeddings\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L11) and its specialized subclasses \(e\.g\., [graph\_embeddings\.py L791](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L791), [graph\_embeddings\.py L849](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L849), [graph\_embeddings\.py L897](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L897)\) that handle coordinate extraction, distance and positional embeddings, and the creation of node and edge features\. These featurization modules are crucial for transforming structural information into a format suitable for the graph neural network architecture\.

 Message passing mechanisms, fundamental to graph neural networks, are implemented through [message\_passing\.py L114](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114) and [message\_passing\.py L227](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py), which update hidden states within the network\. Positional encoding, managed by [positional\_encoding\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py#L5) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py), adds spatial context to the protein residues\.

 The framework supports various stages of model operation, from data preparation to prediction\. For data processing, [mpnn\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L61) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py) constructs a series of transformations to prepare structural data\. This pipeline handles tasks such as filtering, atomization, occupancy masking, and feature aggregation, converting raw structural data into [common\.py L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L106) inputs required by the model\.

 During inference, the [mpnn\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py) orchestrates the process\. It manages model loading and configuration, processes input data through the transformation pipeline, executes the model's forward pass, and decodes sequences\. The inference engine also integrates a [Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-metrics-and-loss-aggregation-framework) for computing metrics such as sequence recovery and confidence scores, and outputs results in formats like CIF and FASTA\.

 For training, the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py) handles the training workflow, extending the [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\. It uses loss functions like [nll\_loss\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) from [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py) and employs a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) for evaluating performance\. Data collation for training utilizes [feature\_collator\.py L187](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py#L187) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py), which efficiently groups examples into batches based on token budget, and [samplers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py#L9) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py) for reproducible and memory\-efficient batch sampling\.### MPNN Models: Core Architectural Components

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN models within Foundry are designed for protein and nucleic acid sequence design using graph neural networks\. At their core, these models, primarily represented by the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py), transform 3D structural data into a graph representation to predict amino acid sequences\.

 A critical initial step involves **graph featurization**, which converts raw atomic coordinates and other structural information into numerical features suitable for a neural network\. This is handled by specialized [graph\_embeddings\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L11) modules in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py)\. For standard protein contexts, [graph\_embeddings\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L11) extracts coordinates, computes pairwise distances, and generates Radial Basis Function \(RBF\) embeddings and positional encodings\. To support diverse design scenarios, specialized subclasses extend this capability: [graph\_embeddings\.py L791](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L791) incorporates membrane\-specific information, [graph\_embeddings\.py L849](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L849) integrates Position\-Specific Scoring Matrix \(PSSM\) features, and [graph\_embeddings\.py L897](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L897) handles complex protein\-ligand interactions by featurizing ligand atoms, their types, and protein\-ligand subgraph edges\. This featurization process also includes adding controlled noise to coordinates to enhance model robustness\.

 Once featurized, the models employ **message passing mechanisms** to propagate information across the protein graph\. [message\_passing\.py L114](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114) and [message\_passing\.py L227](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227), defined in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py), are the primary components for this\. [message\_passing\.py L114](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114) updates both node \(residue\) and edge \(interaction\) hidden states, capturing the structural context\. [message\_passing\.py L227](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227) focuses on updating node hidden states for sequence decoding\. Both layers utilize multi\-layer perceptrons, GELU activations, Layer Normalization, dropout, residual connections, and a [position\_wise\_feed\_forward\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py#L5) network\.

 The [position\_wise\_feed\_forward\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py#L5) network, found in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py), is a standard neural network component that applies two linear transformations separated by an activation function to the hidden representations of nodes, enhancing their expressive power\.

 **Positional encoding**, implemented by the [positional\_encoding\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py#L5) module in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py), provides the model with information about the relative positions of residues and chain identities\. This is crucial for distinguishing interactions between adjacent residues from those far apart in sequence but close in 3D space, and for understanding inter\-chain relationships\.

 During sequence prediction, the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) model orchestrates these components\. It uses encoder layers to build a contextual representation of the protein, and then decodes sequences either in a "teacher\-forcing" manner \(using ground truth for parallel prediction\) or "auto\-regressively" \(iteratively predicting residues based on previous predictions\)\. The model can also incorporate various masks to control which residues are designed and how causality is handled, particularly when dealing with symmetries\. The final step involves converting predicted logits into sampled amino acid sequences, applying biases and temperature parameters to guide the sampling process\. For a detailed explanation of the overall training and inference workflow, refer to [MPNN Models: Training and Inference Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#protein-and-nucleic-acid-biomolecular-modeling-models-mpnn-models-training-and-inference-workflow)\.### MPNN Models: Inference Engine and Workflow

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [mpnn\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) orchestrates the entire inference workflow for ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN models, from loading pre\-trained checkpoints to generating designed protein sequences and structures\. This engine is accessible via a command\-line interface provided by [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py), which parses arguments and converts them into a structured configuration for the engine\.

 At its core, the [mpnn\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) manages the instantiation and loading of model weights for either [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) or [mpnn\.py L2303](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303), ensuring that both legacy and standard PyTorch checkpoints are handled appropriately\. During initialization, the engine validates and processes the provided configuration, ensuring that all parameters, such as model type, output paths, and specific inference settings, are correctly interpreted and standardized\.

 Once configured, the engine processes input data, which can be provided as structured dictionaries or [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects\. It dynamically builds and applies a data transformation pipeline to prepare the structural input for the model\. This pipeline includes steps for feature extraction and annotation necessary for the MPNN models\. The prepared data is then passed through the model in batches, where the forward pass computes probabilities for amino acid sequences\. After the forward pass, the engine decodes the sequences, often involving sampling strategies, and calculates various metrics\. These metrics include [sequence\_recovery\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L14) to assess how well the predicted sequence matches a target, and [nll\.py L495](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L495) to provide a measure of the model's certainty for each designed residue\. For protein\-ligand interactions, specialized metrics like [sequence\_recovery\.py L294](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L294) and [nll\.py L539](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L539) are computed to evaluate performance at the interface\. See [Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-metrics-and-loss-aggregation-framework) for more general information on metrics\.

 The [mpnn\.py L38](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) also handles the output generation\. Designed sequences and associated confidence scores are annotated back onto the [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects\. Unnecessary atoms are then removed before saving the results\. The engine can output designed structures in CIF format and sequences in FASTA format, embedding relevant annotations and metadata for downstream analysis\. The system is designed to be device\-agnostic, automatically utilizing available hardware like CUDA, XPU, or MPS, and gracefully falling back to CPU if specialized hardware is not detected\. Reproducibility is maintained through optional per\-input random number generator seeding\. For a detailed understanding of the overall model architecture, refer to [MPNN Models: Core Architectural Components](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#sequence-design-models-mpnn-mpnn-models-core-architectural-components)\.### MPNN Models: Training Process and Batching Strategies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The training process for MPNN models, encompassing ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN, is orchestrated by the training script located at [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py)\. This script manages the overall workflow, from data preparation and batching strategies to model initialization and optimization\.

 A critical aspect of efficient MPNN training is the handling of variable\-length input sequences\. This is addressed through token\-budgeted batch sampling, implemented by the [samplers\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py#L9) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py)\. This sampler groups samples with similar token lengths into batches, minimizing the computational overhead associated with padding\. It ensures that the product of the longest sequence length in a batch and the batch size remains within a defined [train\.py L211](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L211) limit\. This design choice directly optimizes memory usage and computation time by reducing the amount of padded data processed by the model\. Complementing this, the [feature\_collator\.py L187](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py#L187) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py) further refines batch creation by sorting and pruning examples to adhere to the token budget constraint before performing the actual collation\. This collation process ensures that all features within a batch are consistently padded and formatted for the neural network\.

 The core training logic is encapsulated within the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21), defined in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py)\. This trainer extends the base [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) \(see [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\), providing a specialized framework for MPNN models\. It handles model instantiation, loss computation, and metric tracking\. For sequence prediction tasks, the trainer employs [nll\_loss\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) from [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py)\. This loss function incorporates label smoothing, which helps to prevent model overconfidence and improve generalization by distributing probability mass across possible amino acid labels\.

 The [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) is also configured with a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) to compute and track various evaluation metrics during both training and validation\. These metrics typically include Negative Log Likelihood \(NLL\) and Sequence Recovery, with specialized versions for polymer\-ligand interfaces in the case of LigandMPNN models\. The training process leverages an Adam optimizer and can utilize NoamOpt\-style learning rate schedulers to dynamically adjust the learning rate throughout training, further enhancing stability and convergence\. During training steps, the [mpnn\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) manages forward and backward passes, ensuring gradients are computed efficiently, particularly in distributed training environments\. It also incorporates numerical stability checks to prevent issues like NaN values from propagating through the network\.### MPNN Models: Data Transformation Pipelines

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Data transformation pipelines within the Foundry framework prepare structural data for MPNN models, ensuring consistent and appropriate input for sequence design tasks\. The primary function responsible for constructing these pipelines is [mpnn\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L61) in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py)\. This function orchestrates a series of [README\.md?plain=1 L453](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L453) operations, which are applied conditionally based on whether the pipeline is intended for training or inference, and for specific model types such as [all\.ipynb L154](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L154) or [all\.ipynb L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L155)\.

 The transformation process involves several key stages:

 - **Conditional Routing**: Transforms can be applied selectively using mechanisms like [pipelines\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L115), [pipelines\.py L122](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L122), and [mpnn\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L54)\. This ensures that specific steps are executed only when relevant—for instance, certain augmentations might only apply during training\.
- **Filtering**: Initial steps clean the structural data\. This includes removing hydrogen atoms and filtering out undesired residue tokens or unresolved structural elements that might interfere with model processing\.
- **Atomization**: Residues and other components are processed to define their atomic composition\. This stage includes flagging and reassigning covalent modifications and atomizing non\-polymeric components, distinguishing between standard and unknown amino acid types\.
- **Occupancy Masking**: Residues with unresolved or missing backbone atoms are identified and masked based on specified occupancy thresholds\. This step is crucial for maintaining data quality and preventing the model from processing incomplete structural information\.
- **Featurization**: This stage generates the actual input features for the MPNN models\. This involves: - [mpnn\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L14) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py)\): Encodes non\-atomized tokens into core MPNN features, including coordinates, atom occupancy masks, and sequence encodings, using predefined token orderings such as [token\_encodings\.py L117](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/token_encodings.py#L117) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/token_encodings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/token_encodings.py)\)\. - [mpnn\.py L89](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L89) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py)\): Adds residue indices, chain labels, and residue masks for non\-atomized tokens\. - [mpnn\.py L144](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L144) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py)\): Extracts atomic coordinates and atomic numbers for atomized tokens, particularly relevant for [all\.ipynb L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L155)\. - [user\_settings\.py L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py#L21) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py)\): Integrates user\-defined settings, such as structure noise, decoding type, and causality patterns, directly into the feature set\. - [polymer\_ligand\_interface\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L16) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py)\): Generates a residue\-level mask indicating which polymer residues are at the interface with a ligand, using annotations derived from [polymer\_ligand\_interface\.py L17](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L17) \(in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py)\)\.
- **Finalization**: The processed data is converted into [common\.py L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/common.py#L106) objects and moved to the appropriate device \(CPU, GPU, XPU\)\. The output dictionary is then pruned to include only the necessary [mpnn\.py L174](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L174) and [engine\.py L92](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L92) for model consumption\.

 These transformation pipelines ensure that the MPNN models receive standardized, clean, and comprehensively featurized input, which is essential for accurate protein sequence design\.### MPNN Models: Metrics and Evaluation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides a suite of PyTorch\-based metrics specifically designed for evaluating the performance of MPNN models\. These metrics primarily focus on assessing the accuracy of sequence prediction and the confidence associated with these predictions, with specialized capabilities for analyzing sampled sequences and residues at polymer\-ligand interfaces\. The core metric computations are handled within [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics)\.

 Negative Log Likelihood \(NLL\) and perplexity are fundamental metrics for evaluating how well a model predicts a sequence\. The base [nll\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L14) class in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py) calculates these values, with subclasses extending its functionality\. For instance, [nll\.py L397](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L397) adapts the NLL calculation for sequences that are sampled \(designed\) by the model rather than being directly provided as ground truth\. This is crucial for evaluating the generative capabilities of the MPNN models\. Furthermore, [nll\.py L222](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L222) and [nll\.py L442](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L442) provide NLL and perplexity specifically for residues located at the polymer\-ligand interface, offering insights into interaction design accuracy\. These interface\-specific metrics use [nll\.py L234](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L234) to identify relevant residues and combine this information with masks to focus the evaluation\.

 Confidence scores, such as those provided by [nll\.py L495](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L495) and [nll\.py L539](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L539), are derived from NLL values and reflect the model's certainty in its predictions\. [nll\.py L495](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L495) wraps [nll\.py L397](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L397) to convert NLL into confidence per example and per residue\. Similarly, [nll\.py L539](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L539) applies this logic to interface\-specific predictions\.

 Sequence recovery accuracy, defined by the [sequence\_recovery\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L14) class in [`models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py), measures the percentage of correctly predicted residues\. This metric is computed by comparing the model's sampled or argmax\-predicted sequences against the ground truth\. [sequence\_recovery\.py L294](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L294) extends this by focusing solely on the sequence recovery of residues within the polymer\-ligand interface, providing a targeted assessment of the model's ability to design interacting regions\.
