 The [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) \(described in [Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-metrics-and-loss-aggregation-framework)\) orchestrates the computation of these metrics, allowing for flexible input mapping and tag\-based conditional computation\. This framework ensures that appropriate metrics are applied based on the specific context of the model and the task\.

 For details on the model architectures that these metrics evaluate, see [MPNN Models: Core Architectural Components](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#sequence-design-models-mpnn-mpnn-models-core-architectural-components)\. The data transformation pipelines that prepare input for these models are discussed in [MPNN Models: Data Transformation Pipelines](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#sequence-design-models-mpnn-mpnn-models-data-transformation-pipelines)\.## All\-Atom Structure Prediction \(RF3\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) is a deep learning model designed for *de novo* all\-atom biomolecular structure prediction, including proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules, along with their interactions\. The framework supports the prediction of arbitrary biomolecules and covalent modifications\. It integrates advanced features such as implicit chirality representations and atom\-level geometric conditioning during training, which contribute to its performance in predicting chiral ligands and in scenarios like fixed\-backbone or fixed\-conformer docking\.

 RF3 provides a command\-line interface \(CLI\) for inference, allowing users to run structure predictions with diverse input types\. These inputs can range from JSON configurations specifying sequences and components to [README\.md?plain=1 L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L119) files and MSA inputs \([README\.md?plain=1 L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L94) or [README\.md?plain=1 L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L94)\)\. The CLI supports batch predictions to optimize for startup costs and offers extensive configuration options via Hydra for parameters such as early stopping thresholds, checkpoint paths, the number of recycles, diffusion batch size, and the number of diffusion steps\. It also enables templating, where specific structural selections can be provided to guide the prediction process\. Output generation includes structured [README\.md?plain=1 L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L119) files and confidence metrics like pLDDT, which can be annotated onto the [README\.md?plain=1 L614](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L614) column in the output CIF files for visualization\.

 Beyond inference, RF3 includes a comprehensive infrastructure for training and validation\. This infrastructure leverages PyTorch Lightning Fabric for distributed training and integrates specialized loss functions and metrics tailored for all\-atom structure prediction\. The training process supports iterative refinement through a recycler module and evaluates predictions using metrics such as all\-atom LDDT, chiral loss, and predicted aligned error \(PAE\)\. The validation infrastructure ensures robust evaluation of model performance throughout the training lifecycle\.

 For more detailed information on RF3's core architecture and its diffusion process, refer to [RF3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-core-model-architecture-and-diffusion-process)\. Information regarding the RF3 inference engine and CLI usage is available in [RF3: Inference Engine and CLI Usage](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-inference-engine-and-cli-usage)\. For data processing pipelines, see [RF3: Data Processing Pipelines for Diverse Inputs](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-data-processing-pipelines-for-diverse-inputs)\. Details on training and validation can be found in [RF3: Training and Validation Infrastructure](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-training-and-validation-infrastructure)\. Lastly, the testing suite for RF3 is described in [RF3: Testing Suite and CPU\-GPU Parity](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-testing-suite-and-cpu-gpu-parity)\.### RF3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) model for all\-atom biomolecular structure prediction is structured around a core architecture that integrates feature initialization, iterative refinement \(recycling\), a diffusion module for 3D structure prediction, and a distogram head\. An extended version, [RF3\.py L334](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L334), further incorporates confidence metric prediction and early stopping mechanisms\.

 The primary model, [RF3\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L56), defined in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py), takes inputs and processes them through a [RF3\.py L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L69) to generate initial representations\. These representations then undergo iterative refinement via a [RF3\_structure\.py L257](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L257) module before being fed into the [RF3\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L71), which is responsible for the actual 3D structure prediction\. Concurrently, a [RF3\.py L72](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L72) predicts inter\-residue distance distributions\. The model's forward pass orchestrates these components, either performing a single denoising step during training or a full diffusion rollout during inference\. The [RF3\.py L221](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L221) method manages the iterative refinement process, yielding intermediate outputs for subsequent stages\.

 At a foundational level, RF3 relies on a comprehensive set of neural network layers\. For example, [af3\_auxiliary\_heads\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py#L25) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py) calculates confidence metrics like pLDDT, PAE, and PDE\. The diffusion process itself is powered by modules like [af3\_diffusion\_transformer\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py#L18), [af3\_diffusion\_transformer\.py L256](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py#L256), and [af3\_diffusion\_transformer\.py L283](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py#L283) from [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_diffusion_transformer.py), which process atom\-level and token\-level features through various attention mechanisms and transformations\. These are built upon basic components such as [attention\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L18) and [attention\.py L157](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L157) \(found in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py)\), which update pair representations\.

 Key components for feature initialization and representation refinement include [pairformer\_layers\.py L401](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L401), [pairformer\_layers\.py L440](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L440), and [pairformer\_layers\.py L467](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L467) from [`models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py)\. These modules prepare and embed initial token and pairwise features, including details like relative positional information and token bond data\. The [pairformer\_layers\.py L572](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L572) in the same directory refines Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) representations by using outer products and weighted averaging\.

 The diffusion sampling process during inference, as detailed in [RF3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-core-model-architecture-and-diffusion-process), is managed by components like [inference\_sampler\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/diffusion_samplers/inference_sampler.py#L11) and [inference\_sampler\.py L206](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/diffusion_samplers/inference_sampler.py#L206) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/diffusion_samplers/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/diffusion_samplers/inference_sampler.py)\. These samplers construct noise schedules and iteratively denoise structures to generate the final atomic coordinates\.

 Overall, RF3's architecture is characterized by its modular design, allowing for the integration of specialized components for feature processing, iterative refinement, diffusion\-based prediction, and confidence estimation, all contributing to its capability for all\-atom structural prediction\. For more details on the individual neural network building blocks, refer to [Neural Network Building Blocks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#neural-network-building-blocks)\.### RF3: Data Processing Pipelines for Diverse Inputs

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) model relies on sophisticated data processing pipelines to prepare diverse biomolecular structural inputs for all\-atom structure prediction\. These pipelines, primarily orchestrated through [pipelines\.py L129](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L129) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py), transform raw [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) inputs into the complex features required by deep learning models\.

 The initial stages of data processing involve cleaning and normalizing the input structures\. This includes removing elements like hydrogens and terminal oxygens, filtering out incomplete or undesirable units, and handling chemical modifications\. A key aspect is the atomization process, where molecules are broken down into their atomic components and optionally re\-assigned based on chemical descriptors\. Essential structural annotations, such as global atom and residue identifiers, are added to maintain molecular context throughout the pipeline\.

 Data augmentation techniques are employed to enhance model robustness and generalization\. These include spatial and contiguous cropping strategies and random mirroring of inputs, designed to introduce variability while preserving structural integrity\. The system also supports detailed feature generation, which is a comprehensive step\. It involves loading and subsampling cached residue\-level data, encoding token\-level features, and generating features from reference molecules\. Critical molecular properties, such as atom\-level embeddings, molecular automorphisms, and chiral features derived from chemical libraries like RDKit, are computed\. Cyclic peptide bonds are also detected and integrated into the feature set\. For multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\), the pipeline handles their loading, pairing, merging, and encoding into model\-ready features\.

 A significant portion of the pipeline is dedicated to diffusion\-specific preprocessing\. This involves copying annotations, precisely positioning unresolved atoms, batching structures for diffusion noising, and sampling noise according to specific distributions\. The [pipeline\_utils\.py L45](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py#L45) function in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py) creates noised ground truth template distograms by adding Gaussian noise to token centers, calculating pairwise distances, and discretizing them\. This is crucial for training diffusion models\. Additionally, the pipeline generates features specifically for the confidence heads, used to predict metrics like pLDDT and PAE, by encoding atom arrays and adding relevant annotations\. The overall data processing framework leverages generic utilities for flexible pipeline construction, ensuring that the processed data is suitable for subsequent model training or inference\.### RF3: Training and Validation Infrastructure

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Training and validation for RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) are managed through a comprehensive infrastructure designed to handle distributed training, specialized loss functions, and a variety of evaluation metrics\. The primary entry points are [README\.md?plain=1 L124](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L124) and [train\.py L132](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py#L132) within the [`models/rf3/src/rf3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3) directory, which leverage [train\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py#L25) for configuration and [all\.ipynb L84](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L84) for orchestrating distributed operations\.

 The [rf3\.py L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L35) class, located in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers), serves as the core component for general RF3\-style model training\. It is responsible for setting up training parameters such as the number of recycles and the recycle schedule, instantiating the deep learning model, and optionally applying Exponential Moving Average \(EMA\)\. During both training and validation steps, it prepares network inputs, performs shape assertions, and handles NaN values\. It also assembles ground truth data and metadata for loss and metric computations\. A key feature is the integration of symmetry resolution through [af3\_losses\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L56) and [af3\_losses\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L10), which align predicted structures with ground truth by addressing symmetries at the residue and subunit levels\.

 For models that include a confidence head, [rf3\.py L361](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L361) \(also in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers)\) extends [rf3\.py L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L35)\. This specialized trainer focuses on training the confidence prediction components, often freezing other model parameters\. It performs "mini\-rollouts" during training and "FULL rollouts" during validation to assess confidence\-related metrics, using specific loss functions for [all\.ipynb L231](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L231), [all\.ipynb L231](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L231), and [all\.ipynb L300](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L300) prediction\. This distinction highlights the model's ability to not only predict structures but also quantify its confidence in those predictions\.

 A diverse set of loss functions, defined in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/loss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss), are used to guide the training process\. These include [af3\_confidence\_loss\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L18) for evaluating the model's confidence predictions \(e\.g\., pLDDT, PAE, PDE\), [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) for coordinate prediction \(including mean squared error and smoothed lDDT\), and [af3\_losses\.py L628](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L628) for evaluating predicted distance histograms\. Additionally, [af3\_losses\.py L362](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L362) and [chiral\.py L158](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L158) address specific structural properties\.

 Model evaluation is performed using an extensive suite of metrics, implemented in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics)\. These metrics quantify various aspects of structural accuracy and quality\. Examples include [lddt\.py L205](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L205), [lddt\.py L268](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L268), and [lddt\.py L371](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L371) for assessing local structural accuracy; [chiral\.py L158](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L158) for quantifying errors related to chirality; and [predicted\_error\.py L43](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L43) and [predicted\_error\.py L73](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L73) for predicted TM\-score and interface TM\-score\. Other metrics such as [clashing\_chains\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py#L10), [distogram\.py L178](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L178), [distogram\.py L317](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L317), [rasa\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/rasa.py#L9), and [selected\_distances\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/selected_distances.py#L13) provide comprehensive insights into the quality of predicted structures\.

 Callback mechanisms, detailed in [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system), are integrated to manage various aspects of the training and validation process\. Specifically, the [dump\_validation\_structures\.py L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py#L19) in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks) handles saving predicted structures and diffusion trajectories, which is particularly useful for visualizing model outputs\. The [metrics\_logging\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/metrics_logging.py#L16) collects and aggregates validation metrics across distributed ranks, persisting them to CSV files\. The [metrics\_logging\.py L218](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/metrics_logging.py#L218) then logs these aggregated metrics to provide insights into model performance\. These callbacks ensure that valuable information is captured and managed throughout the training lifecycle\.### RF3: Inference Engine and CLI Usage

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The command\-line interface \(CLI\) for RosettaFold3 \(RF3\) structure prediction is provided via the [README\.md?plain=1 L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L91) command, enabling users to initiate protein folding processes\. This CLI, implemented in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py) using [pyproject\.toml L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L35) and [pyproject\.toml L27](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L27), handles logging configuration, resolves Hydra configuration paths, and parses command\-line arguments\. It distinguishes between a single input file and Hydra overrides, automatically adding [cli\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py#L58) if not specified\. The [inference\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference.py#L32) function from [`models/rf3/src/rf3/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference.py) is called to execute the prediction, with heavy dependencies imported lazily to optimize CLI startup times\. The [cli\.py L75](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py#L75) command serves as an alias for [cli\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py#L12), providing an alternative command name\.

 The core of the RF3 inference process is managed by the [rf3\.py L225](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L225), defined in [`models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py)\. This engine orchestrates model loading, data preprocessing, and output generation\. Its [ddp\.py L64](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L64) method handles configuration overrides and dynamic loading of MSA directories\. The [base\.py L129](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py#L129) method configures a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) for RF3\-specific metrics like [all\.ipynb L231](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L231), [all\.ipynb L302](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L302), and [rf3\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L54)\. The [engine\.py L207](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L207) method is the main entry point for predictions, accepting various input types such as [inference\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L62) objects, [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects, or file paths, which are converted into [inference\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L62) objects\.

 To support distributed inference, the engine utilizes [inference\.py L650](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L650) and [datasets\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/datasets.py#L7) to ensure balanced data loading across different ranks\. An optional early stopping mechanism can terminate predictions if the mean pLDDT score falls below a specified threshold, as determined by [rf3\.py L203](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L203)\.

 Output generation involves transforming raw model outputs into [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects using [io\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py#L61)\. Confidence scores, such as pLDDT, pAE, and pDE, are compiled into AlphaFold3\-compatible [rf3\.py L107](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L107) and [rf3\.py L108](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L108)\. If an output directory is specified, results are saved in an AlphaFold3\-compatible format, organized by example ID and sample index\. This involves functions like [rf3\.py L149](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L149) and [rf3\.py L167](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L167)\. If no output directory is provided, results are accumulated in memory as [rf3\.py L99](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L99) objects and gathered across distributed ranks\. The [rf3\.py L99](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L99) dataclass stores the predicted [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20), [rf3\.py L107](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L107), and optional [rf3\.py L108](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py#L108), and provides a [engine\.py L98](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L98) method for saving these results to disk\.

 The RF3 documentation in [`models/rf3/README.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md) details how to install the [RF3\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L56) package, download model checkpoints, and use the [README\.md?plain=1 L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L91) command\. It covers various input formats, including JSON configurations for sequences and components, [README\.md?plain=1 L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L119) files, and [README\.md?plain=1 L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L94) or [README\.md?plain=1 L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L94) files for MSAs\. The documentation also explains how to handle batch predictions, arbitrary biomolecules, covalent modifications, and templating using [inference\.py L68](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L68) and [inference\.py L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L69) with [README\.md?plain=1 L433](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L433) syntax\. Command\-line arguments like [README\.md?plain=1 L138](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L138), [engine\.py L45](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L45), [README\.md?plain=1 L582](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L582), [engine\.py L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L48), [README\.md?plain=1 L586](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L586), [engine\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L80), and [README\.md?plain=1 L614](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L614) are also described for fine\-tuning prediction behavior\.

 For more details on the RF3 model architecture and diffusion process, refer to [RF3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-core-model-architecture-and-diffusion-process)\. Information on data processing pipelines can be found in [RF3: Data Processing Pipelines for Diverse Inputs](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#all-atom-structure-prediction-rf3-rf3-data-processing-pipelines-for-diverse-inputs)\.### RF3: Testing Suite and CPU\-GPU Parity

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RF3 model incorporates a comprehensive testing suite to ensure the reliability and correctness of its all\-atom structure prediction capabilities\. This suite includes both unit tests, which validate individual components, and integration tests, which verify end\-to\-end functionality, CLI options, and the reproducibility of results\. A key aspect of this testing is the validation of CPU\-GPU parity for confidence metrics, leveraging GPU\-generated baselines for robust verification\.

 The integration tests, located in [`models/rf3/tests/integration`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration), focus on the [README\.md?plain=1 L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L91) command\-line interface\. These tests ensure that the CLI correctly processes diverse input formats, including protein\-only JSON, protein\-ligand JSON, and protein\-ligand CIF files\. Command\-line options such as [engine\.py L51](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L51), [README\.md?plain=1 L138](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L138), [README\.md?plain=1 L614](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L614), [engine\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L80), [inference\.py L68](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L68), and [inference\.py L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L69) are verified by various tests in [`models/rf3/tests/integration/test_options.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/test_options.py)\. Reproducibility is confirmed by [test\_options\.py L73](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/test_options.py#L73) in [`models/rf3/tests/integration/test_options.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/test_options.py), which ensures that identical runs with the same [engine\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L80) yield consistent results\. The [`models/rf3/tests/integration/conftest.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/conftest.py) in this directory provides shared fixtures and helper functions like [conftest\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/conftest.py#L83) to execute the CLI with optimized speed flags for continuous integration environments, and [conftest\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/conftest.py#L155) to manage model checkpoint availability\.

 A critical component of the integration testing is the CPU\-GPU parity check, detailed in [`models/rf3/tests/integration/test_cpu_gpu_parity.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/test_cpu_gpu_parity.py)\. This test, specifically [test\_cpu\_gpu\_parity\.py L77](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/integration/test_cpu_gpu_parity.py#L77), compares scalar confidence metrics \(e\.g\., [all\.ipynb L298](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L298), [all\.ipynb L231](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L231), [all\.ipynb L302](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L302), [all\.ipynb L240](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L240)\) from CPU inference against pre\-committed GPU baselines stored in [`models/rf3/tests/data`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/data)\. This comparison ensures that prediction quality remains consistent across different hardware configurations, with an allowed tolerance for floating\-point differences\.

 Unit tests, distributed throughout the [`models/rf3/tests`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests) directory, cover the core algorithms and neural network components\. For instance, [`models/rf3/tests/test_af3_loss_symmetry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_af3_loss_symmetry.py) validates symmetry resolution functions like [af3\_losses\.py L60](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L60) and [af3\_losses\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L11) used in loss calculations, while [`models/rf3/tests/test_af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_af3_losses.py) ensures the accuracy of [af3\_losses\.py L599](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L599) and [af3\_losses\.py L544](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L544)\. [`models/rf3/tests/test_attention.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_attention.py) verifies the behavior of [attention\.py L18](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L18) and [attention\.py L157](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/attention.py#L157) layers in their vanilla PyTorch implementation \(CPU\-only\)\. Chirality metrics are thoroughly tested by [chiral\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L16) and [chiral\.py L85](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L85) in [`models/rf3/tests/test_chiral.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_chiral.py), and by [test\_chiral\_metrics\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_chiral_metrics.py#L9) in [`models/rf3/tests/test_chiral_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_chiral_metrics.py) under various conditions, including masked atoms and inverted stereocenters\. The [`models/rf3/tests/test_clashing_chains.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_clashing_chains.py) module verifies the [clashing\_chains\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py#L10) metric for detecting clashes between polymer chains\. Distogram calculations and masking are validated by [distogram\.py L120](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L120) and [distogram\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/distogram.py#L155) in [`models/rf3/tests/test_distogram.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_distogram.py), and utilities for building rigid frames by [frames\.py L30](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/frames.py#L30), [frames\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/frames.py#L7), [frames\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/frames.py#L11), and [frames\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/frames.py#L71) in [`models/rf3/tests/test_frames.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_frames.py)\. The conversion between noise scales and noise levels, as well as probability distribution wrapping, are validated by [ground\_truth\_template\.py L124](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py#L124), [ground\_truth\_template\.py L153](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py#L153), and [ground\_truth\_template\.py L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py#L81) in [`models/rf3/tests/test_ground_truth_template.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/test_ground_truth_template.py)\.

 The overall pytest configuration, specified in [`models/rf3/tests/conftest.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/tests/conftest.py), manages test data directories and selectively ignores cluster\-dependent tests to streamline execution in different environments\. This structured approach ensures that RF3's complex biomolecular modeling functionalities are rigorously validated for accuracy, robustness, and consistent performance across diverse computational settings\.## De Novo Biomolecular Interaction Design \(RFdiffusion3\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\) is a diffusion\-based deep learning model within the Foundry framework designed for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design\. This model allows for the creation of novel protein structures under specified constraints, facilitating tasks such as designing protein binders, enzyme active sites, and interfaces with small molecules or nucleic acids\. RFD3's capabilities extend to training, inference, evaluation, and handling complex conditioning requirements\.

 The model's core architecture, defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py), integrates a [encoders\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36), a [RF3\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L71), and an [engine\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54)\. This setup enables conditional generation and classifier\-free guidance during the design process\. The [RFD3\_diffusion\_module\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py) handles the iterative denoising of atom coordinates and predicts sequence information from structural data, employing various neural network layers and recycling loops to refine predictions\. [Neural Network Building Blocks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#neural-network-building-blocks) provides more general information on common architectural components\. The inference process is managed by an [engine\.py L139](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L139) \([`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py)\), which orchestrates the workflow from input processing to model execution and output generation\.

 RFD3 supports diverse design tasks by allowing users to specify constraints through JSON or YAML configuration files\. These constraints can include defining desired binder lengths, referencing target chains, specifying atom\- or residue\-level interaction sites \(hotspots\), and incorporating hydrogen bond conditions\. The model can also enforce symmetry during the diffusion process, enabling the design of symmetric biomolecular assemblies\. Detailed input specifications are covered in [`models/rfd3/docs/input.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/docs/input.md), and an example of its application can be found in [RFdiffusion3: Inference Engine and Input Specification](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-biomolecular-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3-rfdiffusion3-inference-engine-and-input-specification)\.

 The training framework for RFD3 is built on PyTorch Lightning Fabric, allowing for distributed training and efficient resource utilization\. The [rfd3\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) \([`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py)\) extends a base trainer \([`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/fabric_trainer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/fabric_trainer.py)\) to manage the specific needs of amino acid design, including loss calculation, metric gathering, and checkpointing\. Training can be performed on public protein databases \(PDB\) or custom datasets\. During training, RFD3 generates 'problems' by randomizing 'motif tokens' and subsetting them to fix specific atoms, sequences, coordinates, or sequence indices, thereby allowing it to learn from a wide array of conditioning tasks\. For more information on the model training harness, see [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\.

 Evaluation of RFD3 designs relies on a suite of metrics defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics)\. These metrics assess various structural and chemical properties, such as backbone quality, presence of clashes, secondary structure composition, sequence recovery, and hydrogen bond statistics\. Loss functions like [losses\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L7) and [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) are used during training to guide the model towards optimal designs\. [Model Evaluation Metrics Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-evaluation-metrics-framework) gives a general overview of this framework\.

 Practical application of RFD3 is supported through various tutorials and examples \([`models/rfd3/docs/tutorials`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/docs/tutorials)\)\. These guides cover common design tasks such as protein binder design, small molecule binder design, nucleic acid binder design, and enzyme design\. The tutorials walk users through input preparation, configuration file setup, execution on high\-performance computing \(HPC\) systems \(e\.g\., via Slurm\), and analysis of output files, including [README\.md?plain=1 L620](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L620) for structures and [README\.md?plain=1 L67](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/README.md?plain=1#L67) for metrics\. The tutorials also address considerations like balancing designability and diversity by adjusting inference parameters\. The extensive documentation within [`models/rfd3/docs`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/docs) provides further details on configuring and applying RFD3 for diverse biomolecular design challenges\.### RFdiffusion3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\) model within Foundry provides a diffusion\-based framework for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design\. At its core, the [RFD3\.py L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py#L19) class, defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py), acts as a high\-level orchestrator\. This class coordinates the [encoders\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36), [RF3\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L71), and [engine\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) to manage conditional generation and classifier\-free guidance, supporting both training and inference operations\.

 The central component for denoising atom coordinates and predicting sequence information is the [RFD3\_diffusion\_module\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32), located in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py)\. This module incorporates various sub\-modules, including [blocks\.py L439](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L439) for sequence prediction, [blocks\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L7) for positional encoding, and specialized transformer blocks like [blocks\.py L638](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L638), [encoders\.py L304](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L304), [blocks\.py L585](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L585), and [blocks\.py L710](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L710)\. These components work together to process noisy atom coordinates and structural features, iteratively refining the predictions\. The module also handles position scaling and can implement a recycling loop to enhance prediction quality\.

 Inference sampling is managed by the [engine\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) system, detailed in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py)\. This system provides classes such as [inference\_sampler\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L58) and [inference\_sampler\.py L363](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L363), which implement the iterative denoising process\. [inference\_sampler\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L58) focuses on core denoising, motif fixing, noise injection, and Classifier\-Free Guidance \(CFG\)\. [inference\_sampler\.py L363](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L363) extends this functionality to enforce symmetry constraints during the diffusion process, which is crucial for designing symmetric biomolecular assemblies\. The [inference\_sampler\.py L572](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L572) then dynamically selects the appropriate sampling strategy based on the given configuration\.

 The initial representations for the model are set up by the [encoders\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36), found in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py)\. This component embeds 1D features and atom features, incorporating positional and motif embeddings\. Subsequently, the [encoders\.py L304](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L304), also in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py), refines these token and pairwise representations by integrating diffusion\-related information like distograms and self\-conditioning\.

 Classifier\-Free Guidance \(CFG\), a technique used to improve sample quality, is supported by utility functions in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/cfg_utils.py), which enable modification of conditioning features and atom coordinates\. The neural network architecture leverages various specialized layers, including [attention\.py L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/attention.py#L91) for attention mechanisms, [chunked\_pairwise\.py L17](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py#L17) for memory\-optimized pairwise embeddings, and [blocks\.py L659](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L659) for processing structural information\. These layers, predominantly found within [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers), are designed to handle the complex, hierarchical nature of biomolecular data, enabling efficient and robust *de novo* design\.### RFdiffusion3: Inference Engine and Input Specification

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RFdiffusion3 inference engine \([engine\.py L139](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L139)\) orchestrates the workflow for generating *de novo* biomolecular interactions\. It manages the entire inference process from preparing diverse inputs to executing the diffusion model and saving the structured outputs\. The engine is configured through [engine\.py L44](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L44), a dataclass that encapsulates all operational settings, including paths to model checkpoints, batch sizes, and flags for controlling output behaviors such as trajectory dumping and input validation\.

 The [engine\.py L207](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L207) method of the [engine\.py L139](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L139) serves as the primary entry point for inference\. It accepts various input formats, such as file paths, or objects conforming to the [input\_parsing\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L115) schema, and an output directory\. It first standardizes these inputs by converting them into a unified format and can multiply specifications to generate multiple designs from a single input\. This input processing pipeline leverages the [engine\.py L453](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L453) function, which is responsible for parsing JSON or YAML configuration files, extracting design parameters, applying global arguments, and managing a subset of relevant keys\. This function also ensures that all input file paths are absolute and supports early validation of design specifications using [engine\.py L539](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L539) to catch errors before model execution\.

 A key aspect of the engine is its flexibility in handling complex input specifications\. The [input\_parsing\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L115) Pydantic model provides a validated schema for defining design parameters\. This includes fields for input [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects, contig definitions, unindexed regions, desired lengths, ligands, and symmetry\. It also supports various atom selection mechanisms, such as [input\_parsing\.py L152](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152) or [input\_parsing\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L176), enabling fine\-grained control over the design process\. The model incorporates comprehensive validation and canonicalization logic, ensuring input consistency and standardization before [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects are constructed\. Functions such as [input\_parsing\.py L549](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L549) and [input\_parsing\.py L1287](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L1287) are used to assemble these [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects from contig specifications, handling partial diffusion and managing chain and residue identifiers\. Support for legacy input formats is also provided through [legacy\_input\_parsing\.py L637](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py#L637), ensuring backward compatibility\.

 Atom selection within these [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects is managed by the [parsing\.py L26](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) class, which normalizes diverse input formats into a consistent internal representation for masking specific atoms\. This allows for precise targeting of design regions and constraints\. The system also integrates distributed data loading for efficient, parallel processing during inference, leveraging a [train\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L16) with [datasets\.py L17](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/datasets.py#L17) to manage data distribution across multiple computational resources\. The engine ensures that predicted structures and associated metadata are saved in standardized formats, such as CIF\.gz files for structures and JSON files for metadata, using the [engine\.py L91](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L91) dataclass to encapsulate these results\. When trajectory dumping is enabled, the engine extracts and processes both noisy and denoised trajectories, which can be aligned and subsampled, providing insights into the diffusion process\. For the architectural components of the RFdiffusion3 model, refer to [RFdiffusion3: Core Model Architecture and Diffusion Process](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#de-novo-biomolecular-interaction-design-rfdiffusion3-rfdiffusion3-core-model-architecture-and-diffusion-process)\.### RFdiffusion3: Training Framework and Evaluation Metrics

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RFdiffusion3 training framework is designed to facilitate the *de novo* generation of biomolecular interactions\. The primary entry point for training is the script in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py), which uses Hydra for configuration management and PyTorch Lightning Fabric for distributed training\. This setup allows for flexible experimentation and scalable training across various hardware configurations\. The training process involves instantiating loggers, callbacks, models, optimizers, and learning rate schedulers, all dynamically configured via Hydra\.

 The core training orchestration is handled by the [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) abstract base class, defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/fabric_trainer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/fabric_trainer.py)\. This class manages the entire training lifecycle, including setting up the Lightning Fabric environment, managing the trainer's state \(model, optimizer, scheduler, global step, epoch\), and handling checkpointing for saving and loading training progress\. It also incorporates gradient management techniques such as gradient clipping, skipping non\-finite gradients, and updating Exponential Moving Average \(EMA\) parameters to enhance training stability and efficiency\.

 For amino acid design tasks, the framework extends [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) with the [rfd3\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) class, located in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py)\. This specialized trainer prepares model inputs, specifically handling noisy atom coordinates and other structural and sequence features\. It also manages recycling schedules, which ensure consistent sampling across distributed training environments by controlling the number of inference steps per training batch\.

 A variety of loss functions and metrics are used to guide and evaluate the training process\. The [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py) module includes [losses\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L7) for token\-level cross\-entropy on sequence predictions and [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) for minimizing the mean squared error on atomic coordinates during the diffusion process\. [af3\_losses\.py L416](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) incorporates weighting factors for various atom types and an optional smoothed Local Distance Difference Test \(LDDT\) score to improve structural accuracy\.

 Evaluation metrics are crucial for assessing the quality of designed proteins\. The [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics) directory provides a comprehensive suite for this purpose\. These metrics include:

 - **Design Metrics**: Defined in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py), these metrics evaluate backbone quality, detect clashes, quantify chain breaks, and analyze secondary structure composition\. They also assess protein\-protein interaction \(PPI\) hotspots and measure sequence recovery\.
- **Hydrogen Bond Metrics**: The modules [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_metrics.py) and [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_hbplus_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_hbplus_metrics.py) calculate hydrogen bond statistics and evaluate the accuracy of predicted donors and acceptors against ground truth data\.
- **Sidechain Metrics**: In [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py), these metrics evaluate sidechain quality by comparing predicted sidechain topologies against standard amino acids, identifying unintended bonds, and detecting clashes\.

 The [rfd3\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) also includes functionality for post\-processing model outputs into structured [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects, which involves cleaning up virtual atoms, reassigning unindexed chains, and incorporating detailed metadata\. During validation, the [dump\_validation\_structures\.py L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py#L19) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py) saves predicted structures and diffusion trajectories, facilitating visual inspection and deeper analysis of the model's performance\.### RFdiffusion3: Advanced Conditioning and Data Transformations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

RFdiffusion3 employs sophisticated data processing and transformation pipelines to prepare biomolecular data for its deep learning models\. These pipelines facilitate the creation of design reference features, featurization of atoms, handling of molecular symmetry, incorporation of hydrogen bond information, and various conditioning strategies critical for both training and inference\.

 Core to the data preparation are the [README\.md?plain=1 L453](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L453) classes and utility functions residing in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms)\. These components operate on [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects, which serve as the central data structure for biomolecular information\.

 **Conditioning and Motif Handling**

 RFdiffusion3 utilizes advanced conditioning mechanisms, which are managed by components such as [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py), [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_utils.py), and [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py)\.

 The system supports diverse training conditions through a class\-based approach\. For instance, [training\_conditions\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) allows for the selection of residue "islands" as motifs, enabling options to diffuse sidechains, sample subgraphs, or fix sequences and coordinates\. [training\_conditions\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) specifically tailors the conditioning for protein\-protein interactions, designating a target protein as a motif with fixed properties\. Subtype conditioning, handled by [training\_conditions\.py L272](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L272), allows models to condition on specific molecular types like ligands or DNA\. Additionally, [conditioning\_base\.py L315](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) within [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py) manages the expansion of "unindexed" motif tokens and generates attention masks to control information flow\.

 **Structural Annotation and Featurization**

 The framework includes transformations for detailed structural annotation and featurization\. Files like [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py) and [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms) contain various featurization [README\.md?plain=1 L453](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/README.md?plain=1#L453)s\. [design\_transforms\.py L117](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L117) generates atom\-level reference features, such as [rf3\.yaml L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/configs/model/rf3.yaml#L14) and [rf3\.yaml L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/configs/model/rf3.yaml#L16)\. [design\_transforms\.py L346](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L346) adds attributes like binned relative solvent accessibility \(RASA\) and active donor/acceptor flags\. Boolean masks for structural roles, such as [pipelines\.py L504](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py#L504) or [losses\.py L104](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L104), are added by [design\_transforms\.py L399](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L399), which internally calls [util\_transforms\.py L220](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py#L220) and [util\_transforms\.py L251](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py#L251) from [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py)\. This ensures that the model receives rich, context\-aware information about each atom and residue\.

 **Hydrogen Bond Calculation**

 RFdiffusion3 integrates hydrogen bond information into its transformations\. [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py) and [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py) in [`models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms) implement methods for calculating hydrogen bonds\.
