The handling of protein residue contigs and motifs in symmetric contexts is also verified in [`models/rfd3na/tests/test_rfd3na_symmetry_contigs.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/tests/test_rfd3na_symmetry_contigs.py)\. Geometry helper functions for symmetry frames, Kabsch superposition, and RMSD calculations are tested in [`models/rfd3na/tests/test_rfd3na_symmetry_frames.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/tests/test_rfd3na_symmetry_frames.py) to ensure their accuracy\.

 Regression testing is a crucial part of the infrastructure\. The [`models/rfd3na/tests/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/tests/transforms) directory, specifically [`models/rfd3na/tests/transforms/test_pipeline_regression.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/tests/transforms/test_pipeline_regression.py), ensures consistent output across various configurations and execution modes by comparing [engine\.py L92](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L92) and [rf3\.py L117](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L117) against pre\-stored regression data\. Legacy pipeline equivalence tests in [`models/rfd3na/tests/test_legacy_pipeline_equivalence.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/tests/test_legacy_pipeline_equivalence.py) verify that new and old implementations produce identical results\.

 For debugging purposes, the [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing) directory provides specialized tools\. The [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/debug.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/debug.py) module facilitates debugging of the model's forward passes and conditional inference scenarios, leveraging Hydra for configuration and handling accelerator setup\. Utility functions in [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/debug_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/debug_utils.py) support manipulating [all\.ipynb L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects and generating CIF files for visual inspection of pipeline outputs\. This includes functions to reconstruct [engine\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L13) objects, save processed structures, and modify pipelines to remove random augmentations for deterministic debugging\.

 The [`models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/testing_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/testing/testing_utils.py) module offers utilities for managing test environments, configurations, example data, and assertions\. It handles loading configurations for inference, training, and validation; managing test data from JSON files; and constructing data pipelines\. It also includes assertion utilities for comparing tensors and NumPy arrays with specified tolerances, and sets up logging and random seeds for reproducibility\.## Foundry CLI Utilities and Model Checkpoint Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides command\-line interface \(CLI\) utilities for managing model checkpoints, facilitating their installation, listing, and cleanup\. These utilities are primarily defined within the [`src/foundry_cli`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli) directory\.

 The core of the CLI functionality is a [pyproject\.toml L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L35)\-based application that enables users to interact with model checkpoints\. This includes commands for:

 - **Installation**: Users can install specific models, all registered models, or a subset of base models\. The installation process involves determining appropriate directories for checkpoints and then downloading the model files\. A crucial aspect of this process is the SHA256 hash verification performed during download to ensure the integrity and authenticity of the installed models\. If a checkpoint already exists, it will not be re\-downloaded unless explicitly forced\.
- **Listing**: The CLI can list all models currently registered within Foundry, providing descriptions for each\. It can also scan designated checkpoint directories to identify and list all installed checkpoints, along with their file sizes\.
- **Cleanup**: A cleanup command allows users to remove all downloaded checkpoints from the discovered directories\. This operation typically includes a confirmation prompt to prevent accidental deletion\.

 The system relies on a centralized registry, [checkpoint\_registry\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L80), to store metadata about available models, including download URLs and expected SHA256 hashes\. Environment variables are integrated to allow for flexible configuration of checkpoint directories\. The use of [download\_checkpoints\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py#L11) provides visual feedback during file downloads, enhancing the user experience\.

 For more details on how these checkpoints are managed and integrated into the overall Foundry inference workflow, refer to [Checkpoint Management and Registry](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-checkpoint-management-and-registry)\.### Checkpoint Registration and Metadata Management

```
# The REGISTERED_CHECKPOINTS dictionary holds metadata for available models.
# Example structure:
REGISTERED_CHECKPOINTS = {
    "rfd3": CheckpointInfo(
        url="https://...",
        filename="rfd3.ckpt",
        description="RFdiffusion 3",
        sha256="...",
    ),
    # ... other checkpoints
}

# _resolve_checkpoint_dirs determines the search path for checkpoints.
# It prioritizes a user-specified directory and includes default locations.
def _resolve_checkpoint_dirs(checkpoint_dir: Optional[Path]) -> list[Path]:
    checkpoint_dirs = get_default_checkpoint_dirs() # e.g., [Path("~/.foundry/checkpoints")]
    if checkpoint_dir is not None:
        resolved = checkpoint_dir.expanduser().absolute()
        if resolved not in checkpoint_dirs:
            checkpoint_dirs.insert(0, resolved)
        # ... (rest of the implementation for moving to front and persisting to .env)
    return checkpoint_dirs

# Example call:
# This would return a list of paths, with '/my/custom/path' at the beginning
# if specified.
# resolved_dirs = _resolve_checkpoint_dirs(Path("/my/custom/path"))
```

Model metadata, including descriptions and download paths for pre\-trained models, is centrally managed by [checkpoint\_registry\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L80) within [`src/foundry_cli`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli)\. This registry enables the Foundry command\-line interface \(CLI\) to consistently locate and retrieve models\. The [download\_checkpoints\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py#L33) function, also in [`src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py), is responsible for determining the specific file system locations where these models are or should be installed\. It identifies potential installation directories, taking into account user\-specified paths and default Foundry locations, and can update the environment dynamically to ensure models are discoverable\. For more details on the command\-line utilities that leverage this system, refer to [Foundry CLI Utilities and Model Checkpoint Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#foundry-cli-utilities-and-model-checkpoint-management)\.### Checkpoint Installation and Integrity Verification

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The process of installing Foundry model checkpoints involves downloading and verifying their integrity\. The function [download\_checkpoints\.py L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py#L106) within [`src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py) orchestrates this process\. It retrieves specific model details from a centralized registry of available checkpoints, then proceeds to download the file using the [download\_checkpoints\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py#L54) utility\. A critical component of this download process is SHA256 hash verification\. This cryptographic hash check is performed after the download is complete to ensure that the downloaded checkpoint file has not been corrupted or tampered with during transfer, thereby guaranteeing the authenticity and integrity of the installed model\. If the hash verification fails, the downloaded file is automatically removed, preventing the use of a potentially compromised checkpoint\.### Dynamic Configuration via Environment Variables

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Configuration of the Foundry command\-line interface \(CLI\) for managing model checkpoints is dynamically handled through environment variables\. The system leverages [train\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py#L8) from the [pyproject\.toml L84](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L84) package \(as seen in [`src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py)\) to automatically load key\-value pairs from [\.env L2](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.env#L2) files\. This allows for flexible and persistent configuration, such as defining default checkpoint storage locations, without requiring direct modification of the codebase\.

 Furthermore, the [checkpoint\_registry\.py L49](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L49) utility within [`src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry_cli/download_checkpoints.py) dynamically updates the environment variables during runtime\. This capability ensures that newly installed or discovered checkpoint directories are immediately recognized by the system, facilitating proper checkpoint discovery and usage across different CLI operations like listing or installing models\. This approach promotes a modular and user\-friendly configuration experience for managing Foundry's deep learning models\. For a broader understanding of how checkpoints are discovered and managed, refer to [Checkpoint Management and Registry](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-checkpoint-management-and-registry)\.## Extensible Callback System

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry's extensible callback system provides a structured way to inject custom logic and monitoring into the deep learning training and validation loops without altering the core trainer code\. This system is centered around the [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) abstract class, which defines a comprehensive set of hook methods that are invoked at various stages of the training process, from the beginning of a training run to the end of a validation batch\. Implementations of specific callbacks inherit from [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) and override these hooks to perform specialized tasks\.

 A key aspect of this system is its ability to monitor model health during training\. This includes tracking statistics and histograms for model gradients, weights, and activations\. A callback for this purpose uses forward hooks to non\-intrusively capture activation data and collects gradient and weight statistics at specified intervals\. This helps in understanding the stability and learning dynamics of the neural network\.

 The system also facilitates the aggregation and persistence of validation metrics\. During the validation phase, each processing unit \(or rank in a distributed setting\) generates metrics\. A dedicated callback collects these outputs into structured dataframes, aggregates them into a global view, de\-duplicates entries to ensure unique examples are represented only once, and then persists the results to CSV files\. This provides a consolidated record of model performance across validation runs\.

 For analyzing the efficiency of the training process, the callback system incorporates timing analysis\. Callbacks can profile the duration of different stages within a training step, such as data loading, forward and backward passes, and optimizer updates\. These timings are then logged and presented, allowing developers to identify potential bottlenecks and optimize performance\.

 Beyond monitoring and timing, the callback system supports diverse logging of training\-related information\. This includes logging the total and trainable parameters of the model, monitoring dataset sampling ratios to ensure balanced data usage, and tracking learning rates of optimizers\. Specialized callbacks can also log model\-specific details, such as AF3\-specific training losses\. These logging capabilities help in debugging, understanding training progress, and ensuring that models are trained effectively\. The system is designed to operate efficiently in distributed environments, ensuring that operations like logging and hook registration occur only on the primary process, preventing redundant work and maintaining system performance\.### Core Callback System Architecture

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The core of Foundry's extensible callback system is defined by the abstract base class [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9), located in [`src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py)\. This class provides a structured interface that allows developers to inject custom logic into various stages of the training and validation processes without altering the main training loop\. Concrete callback implementations inherit from [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) and override its methods to implement specific functionalities\.

 The [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) class includes a comprehensive set of hook methods that are invoked at different points throughout the model's lifecycle\. These hooks cover the overall training fit, individual training epochs, batch processing, optimizer steps, validation epochs, and checkpoint saving\. For instance, [callback\.py L28](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L28) is called at the beginning of the entire training process, while [callback\.py L53](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L53) is invoked after each training batch is processed\. Similarly, hooks like [callback\.py L86](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L86) and [callback\.py L118](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L118) provide specific points for intervention during validation and model persistence\. Each hook typically receives a [train\.py L287](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L287) object, providing access to the current state and components of the training environment\. This design, inspired by systems like PyTorch Lightning, facilitates modularity and extensibility in managing training workflows\. For concrete implementations of these callbacks, refer to [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\.### Model Health Monitoring with Activation, Gradient, and Weight Tracking

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [health\_logging\.py L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/health_logging.py#L48) callback, defined in [`src/foundry/callbacks/health_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/health_logging.py), monitors the internal state of a PyTorch model during training\. Its purpose is to track and log statistics and histograms for model gradients, weights, and activations\. This information provides insight into the model's health and can help identify issues such as vanishing or exploding gradients, or dead neurons\.

 The tracker integrates with the training process through various hooks provided by the [callback\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/callback.py#L9) system\. For instance, it registers forward hooks on model modules to capture activation data without altering the model's architecture\. To manage resources and prevent memory leaks, these hooks are carefully registered and removed at appropriate points in the training cycle\.

 For distributed training environments, the tracker ensures that logging operations occur only on the global rank\-zero process, preventing redundant output and processing overhead\. It also provides flexible filtering options, allowing users to specify which parameters or modules should be monitored, thereby focusing on areas of particular interest\. This selective monitoring helps to manage the volume of collected data and computational cost\. Further details on the core callback system architecture can be found in [Core Callback System Architecture](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system-core-callback-system-architecture)\.### Validation Metrics Aggregation and Persistence

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [metrics\_logging\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/metrics_logging.py#L16) within [`src/foundry/callbacks/metrics_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/metrics_logging.py) facilitates the systematic collection, aggregation, and persistence of validation metrics during model training, especially in distributed computing environments\. It functions by gathering validation outputs from each parallel process \(rank\) into distinct dataframes\.

 At the conclusion of each validation epoch, these rank\-specific dataframes are saved temporarily\. Subsequently, only the global rank\-zero process loads these individual dataframes, merging them into a consolidated view\. A key aspect of this aggregation is the de\-duplication of entries, ensuring that metrics for a unique example are represented only once in the final dataset, even if processed by multiple ranks\. The aggregated metrics are then appended to a master CSV file, providing a persistent record of the model's performance over time\. Temporary files generated during the process are automatically cleaned up to maintain system hygiene\. This robust mechanism ensures that comprehensive and accurate validation performance data is consistently collected and stored, regardless of the complexity of the distributed training setup\.### Detailed Training and Validation Timing Analysis

```
from lightning.fabric import Fabric
from foundry.callbacks import TimingCallback

# Initialize Fabric (assuming it's already configured)
fabric = Fabric()

# Instantiate TimingCallback with a custom logging frequency
timing_callback = TimingCallback(log_every_n=50)

# Create a list of callbacks to be used during training
# Other callbacks would be added here as needed
callbacks = [timing_callback]

# Example of how you might pass callbacks to a trainer (conceptual)
# trainer = MyTrainer(fabric=fabric, callbacks=callbacks)
# trainer.run(model, dataloader)
```

The [timing\_logging\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/timing_logging.py#L13) is designed to profile and log the duration of various stages within the training and validation loops, providing insights into performance bottlenecks\. It uses a [torch\.py L330](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/torch.py#L330) object to track intervals, such as data loading, forward and backward passes, and optimizer steps\. This callback then aggregates and presents these timings in a formatted table, ensuring that these operations and logging only occur on the global rank\-zero process in distributed training environments\. This mechanism helps in understanding where computational resources are being spent during model training\. This callback is part of the broader [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\.### Diverse Training Information Logging and Monitoring

| Callback Name | Function | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LogModelParametersCallback | Prints a table of total and trainable model parameters at the start of training\. | foundry/callbacks/train\_logging\.py |
| PrintExampleIDBeforeForwardPassCallback | Prints the example ID for each rank at the start of the forward pass for each batch \(debugging only\)\. | foundry/callbacks/train\_logging\.py |
| LogDatasetSamplingRatiosCallback | Monitors and logs the sampling ratios of datasets after each epoch\. | foundry/callbacks/train\_logging\.py |
| LogLearningRateCallback | Logs the learning rate of the optimizer periodically\. | foundry/callbacks/train\_logging\.py |
| LogAF3TrainingLossesCallback | Logs mean training losses, epoch times, and optionally full batch losses for AF3 models\. | foundry/callbacks/train\_logging\.py |

The [pyproject\.toml L95](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L95) framework employs specialized callbacks to provide comprehensive logging and monitoring of diverse training information\. This system, part of the [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system), allows for granular insights into model behavior and training progress\.

 Model parameters are monitored by the [train\_logging\.py L26](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py#L26) which prints a formatted overview of the total and trainable parameters of the model at the start of training, located in [`src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py)\. This provides an immediate summary of model complexity and parameter count\.

 For debugging purposes, the [train\_logging\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py#L33) in [`src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py) logs the [engine\.py L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L94) for each batch before the forward pass, which can be useful for tracing specific data points through the model\. To prevent redundant output in distributed environments, such debugging information is controlled to ensure it only appears on the global rank\-zero process\.

 Dataset sampling ratios are tracked by the [train\_logging\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py#L58), also found in [`src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py)\. This callback monitors and logs the proportion of examples drawn from each dataset after every training epoch\. It provides counts and percentages, offering insight into the effective sampling strategy during training\. The sampling ratios are extracted from [engine\.py L94](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L94) fields, reflecting the framework's approach to identifying data origin\.

 The [train\_logging\.py L93](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py#L93) in [`src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py) records the learning rate of the optimizer at predefined intervals, enabling continuous monitoring of the optimization schedule and dynamic adjustment during training\.

 Finally, for models like AlphaFold3, specialized logging is handled by the [train\_logging\.py L116](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py#L116) in [`src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/callbacks/train_logging.py)\. This callback tracks and logs mean losses per batch and per epoch, measures epoch timings, and can optionally log full batch losses for individual structures\. It utilizes the [pyproject\.toml L31](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/pyproject.toml#L31) library for enhanced console output, presenting training progress and statistics in organized panels and tables\. This detailed logging provides critical information for understanding the model's performance and convergence behavior during complex training runs\.## Model Inference Infrastructure

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides an infrastructure for model inference, designed to separate the setup of a model from its execution\. This separation allows for efficient inference by performing the resource\-intensive setup process only once\. The core of this system resides in the [`src/foundry/inference_engines`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines) directory\.

 The central component is the [base\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py#L33) class, defined in [`src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py)\. This abstract class manages the loading of pre\-trained model checkpoints and their associated configurations\. It supports applying various configuration overrides for transformations, inference sampler settings, and trainer configurations, allowing for customization of the model's behavior at inference time\. The [base\.py L129](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py#L129) method within this class handles the initial setup, including constructing data transformation pipelines and initializing the trainer with the loaded model weights, ensuring that optimizers are not loaded as they are not needed for inference\. The [engine\.py L207](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L207) method, which must be implemented by subclasses, defines the specific inference logic\. The engine also supports context management for proper resource cleanup and includes parameters indicating its support for distributed inference setups\.

 Foundry also provides a comprehensive system for managing and registering model checkpoints\. The [`src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py) file facilitates this by defining default search locations for checkpoints and allowing users to specify additional search paths via environment variables\. It maintains a registry of commonly used checkpoints, including their download URLs and descriptions, enabling easy access and location of pre\-trained models\. This registry uses a [checkpoint\_registry\.py L65](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L65) dataclass to store metadata and a [checkpoint\_registry\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L71) method to locate existing checkpoint files on disk, or determine their expected storage location upon download\. Command\-line interface utilities exist for managing these checkpoints, including installation, listing, and cleanup, which can be explored further in [Foundry CLI Utilities and Model Checkpoint Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#foundry-cli-utilities-and-model-checkpoint-management)\.### Core Inference Engine Architecture and Lifecycle

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The core inference engine within Foundry, built upon the [base\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py#L33) abstract class defined in [`src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py), provides a structured approach to model inference\. This design separates the potentially resource\-intensive setup phase from the actual execution of inference, allowing for efficient and repeatable predictions\.

 The engine orchestrates several key steps:

 1. **Checkpoint Loading and Configuration:** It begins by loading a pre\-trained model checkpoint\. The system supports loading from direct file paths or using a registry of known checkpoints, which can be found in [Checkpoint Management and Registry](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-checkpoint-management-and-registry)\. This checkpoint contains the model's weights and its original training configuration\.
2. **Configuration Merging and Overriding:** To ensure flexibility, the engine allows for extensive customization of the inference process\. Users can specify overrides for the model's behavior, data transformations, inference sampler settings, and even trainer configurations\. These overrides are merged with the loaded checkpoint's configuration, enabling fine\-tuning without modifying the original checkpoint\.
3. **Dynamic Initialization of Components:** Once the final configuration is established, the engine dynamically initializes two crucial components: - **Data Transformation Pipeline:** This pipeline is responsible for preparing raw input data into the format expected by the model\. It extracts transformation settings from the configuration and applies any user\-defined overrides\. - **Trainer:** A [train\.py L287](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L287) instance, derived from [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness), is instantiated and configured specifically for inference\. This involves loading the model weights and ensuring that components relevant only to training, such as optimizers, are not loaded, and the model is set to evaluation mode\.
4. **Inference Execution:** The [engine\.py L207](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L207) method, which is implemented by specific inference engine subclasses \(e\.g\., [MPNN Models: Inference Engine and Workflow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#sequence-design-models-mpnn-mpnn-models-inference-engine-and-workflow)\), then executes the actual inference logic, utilizing the prepared model and data pipeline\.
5. **Context Management and Distributed Inference:** The [base\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py#L33) supports Python's context management protocol, ensuring proper cleanup of resources after inference\. Furthermore, it incorporates mechanisms to support distributed inference setups, allowing for scalable predictions across multiple devices or nodes\.### Checkpoint Management and Registry

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry employs a comprehensive system for managing model checkpoints, allowing for the registration, discovery, and loading of pre\-trained deep learning models\. This system centralizes metadata and provides robust mechanisms for locating checkpoint files, whether they are locally stored or need to be downloaded\.

 The default search paths for checkpoints are established by the [checkpoint\_registry\.py L25](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L25) function in [`src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py)\. This function prioritizes a default local directory \(e\.g\., [README\.md?plain=1 L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/README.md?plain=1#L48)\) and incorporates additional paths specified via the [\.env L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.env#L63) environment variable\. This allows users to customize where the system looks for models\. For persistent configuration, the [checkpoint\_registry\.py L49](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L49) utility allows users to save their preferred checkpoint directories to a [\.env L2](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/.env#L2) file, ensuring these settings are consistently applied across sessions without manual re\-entry\.

 A central registry for known models is maintained through the [checkpoint\_registry\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L80) dictionary, which maps descriptive keys to [checkpoint\_registry\.py L65](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L65) dataclass instances\. Each [checkpoint\_registry\.py L65](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L65) in [`src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py) stores essential metadata such as the model's URL, filename, and a descriptive text\. The [checkpoint\_registry\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py#L71) method associated with this dataclass facilitates locating the actual checkpoint file on disk by searching the configured directories\. This registry streamlines access to frequently used models, simplifying their retrieval and deployment within the Foundry framework\. This robust management system ensures that models can be easily identified, installed, and verified for integrity before use in inference tasks\. Further details on how these checkpoints are loaded and integrated into the inference workflow can be found in [Core Inference Engine Architecture and Lifecycle](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-inference-infrastructure-core-inference-engine-architecture-and-lifecycle)\.## Model Evaluation Metrics Framework

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Foundry framework provides a modular system for evaluating deep learning models, particularly focusing on the aggregation and computation of various loss functions and metrics\. This system allows for flexible definition of custom metrics, dynamic input mapping, and conditional computation based on tags associated with data or tasks\.

 Central to this framework is the concept of a [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40), which orchestrates the computation of multiple [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) objects\. The [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) can be initialized from individual [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) instances or through configuration files, such as those generated by Hydra, as described in [Hydra\-based Configuration and Dynamic Resolution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-hydra-based-configuration-and-dynamic-resolution)\. It processes input data and selectively applies metrics based on defined tags, ensuring that only relevant evaluations are performed\. The [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) also handles the mapping of input arguments to the specific requirements of each [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) through an adapter mechanism, allowing a flexible interface between the raw model outputs and the metric computation logic\. Error handling is integrated to manage potential issues during metric calculation\.

 Custom metrics are defined by inheriting from an abstract [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) class, which establishes a consistent interface for all evaluation components\. Subclasses must implement a [metric\.py L319](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L319) method that performs the actual calculation, returning results in a structured dictionary format\. This design ensures extensibility, allowing developers to easily add new evaluation criteria\. The [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) class also supports conditional execution through properties like [metric\.py L151](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L151), [metric\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L155), and [metric\.py L159](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L159), which enable fine\-grained control over when a metric is applied\.

 For aggregating loss functions, the framework includes a [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class, inheriting from [weights\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20) in [`src/foundry/metrics/losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py)\. This class is designed to combine several individual loss functions into a single total loss\. During initialization, it instantiates various loss functions based on provided configurations\. Its [EMA\.py L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L63) method then iterates through these functions, computing each individual loss, summing their scalar outputs, and merging their detailed results into a dictionary\. This aggregated loss and the detailed dictionary are then returned, providing a comprehensive view of the model's performance with respect to different loss components\. This structure is critical for training processes, as detailed in [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\.### MetricManager for Orchestrated Metric Computation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) class, located in [`src/foundry/metrics/metric.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py), is central to Foundry's model evaluation framework, orchestrating the computation and aggregation of various evaluation metrics\. It functions as a container for multiple [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) objects, enabling flexible and configurable performance assessment\.

 The manager can be initialized from pre\-existing [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) instances or dynamically from Hydra configurations, as demonstrated by [metric\.py L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L16) and the class method [rf3\.py L79](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L79)\. This flexibility supports both programmatic and declarative approaches to metric definition\.

 When invoked, the [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) iterates through its registered [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) instances, determining which metrics to compute based on a tag\-based conditional system\. This system uses [metric\.py L151](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L151), [metric\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L155), and [metric\.py L159](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L159) properties within each [metric\.py L184](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L184) to filter execution\. This allows for selective metric computation relevant to specific experimental conditions or model types\.

 Each individual metric's computation is handled by its [metric\.py L249](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L249) method, which acts as an adapter\. It processes the input arguments, mapping them to the specific parameters required by the metric's [metric\.py L319](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L319) method, using [metric\.py L284](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L284) and [metric\.py L303](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L303) for flexible data extraction from potentially nested input dictionaries\. The results from each metric are then aggregated into a single output dictionary, with unique keys formed by prefixing each metric's name\. Error handling is managed through [metric\.py L164](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L164), allowing for controlled propagation of [metric\.py L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L36) exceptions based on the [metric\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L58) flag set during initialization\. For details on how individual metrics are structured, see [Metrics and Loss Aggregation Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#core-framework-development-metrics-and-loss-aggregation-framework)\.### Loss Function Aggregation and Computation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry's approach to loss function aggregation centers on the [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class, which extends [weights\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20) to manage multiple individual loss functions\. This class instantiates these functions from Hydra configurations, allowing for flexible and modular definition of the overall loss computation\. The [EMA\.py L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/training/EMA.py#L63) method of the [losses\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/losses.py#L8) class iterates through these individual loss functions, calculating each one, accumulating their scalar outputs into a total loss, and merging any additional dictionary results they provide\. This process includes handling appropriate device and data type promotions to ensure consistency across different loss components\. This aggregation is a key part of the [Model Evaluation Metrics Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-evaluation-metrics-framework) within Foundry, particularly as managed by the [metric\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40)\.## Neural Network Building Blocks

```
class FourierEmbedding(nn.Module):
    # w and b are registered buffers
    w: torch.Tensor
    b: torch.Tensor

    def __init__(self, c: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.c = c
        # Initializes w and b with zeros, then calls reset_parameters
        self.register_buffer("w", torch.zeros(c, dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer("b", torch.zeros(c, dtype=torch.float32))
        self.reset_parameters()

    def reset_parameters(self) -> None:
        # Initializes w and b with values from a normal distribution
        nn.init.normal_(self.w)
        nn.init.normal_(self.b)

    def forward(
        self,
        t: torch.Tensor,  # Input tensor, e.g., [D]
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Applies Fourier embedding formula: cos(2 * pi * (t * w + b))
        return torch.cos(2 * pi * (t[..., None] * self.w + self.b))

# Example Usage (not part of the class, for illustration)
# embedder = FourierEmbedding(c=64)
# input_tensor = torch.randn(10)
# output = embedder(input_tensor)
```

Foundry provides core neural network components, including reusable layers for constructing model architectures\. These components are located within [`src/foundry/model`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model) and [`src/foundry/model/layers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers)\.

 One such component is the [blocks\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L7) layer, defined in [`src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py)\. This layer generates Fourier features from an input tensor, mapping it to a higher\-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions with learnable parameters\. The parameters are initialized using a normal distribution and are registered as buffers, meaning they are saved with the model but are not updated during optimization\.

 Another component is the [blocks\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L32) layer, also found in [`src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py)\. This implementation of dropout supports an optional broadcasting mechanism, where the dropout mask can be applied uniformly across a specified dimension\. During training, a Bernoulli distribution generates the mask, which is then applied to the input and scaled to maintain the expected sum of activations\.### Fourier Embedding Layer

```
class FourierEmbedding(nn.Module):
    # w and b are registered as buffers
    w: torch.Tensor
    b: torch.Tensor

    def __init__(self, c: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.c = c
        # Register w and b as buffers, making them part of the model's state
        # but not considered model parameters.
        self.register_buffer("w", torch.zeros(c, dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer("b", torch.zeros(c, dtype=torch.float32))
        self.reset_parameters() # Initialize w and b

    def forward(
        self,
        t: torch.Tensor,  # [D]
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Compute the Fourier embedding using a cosine function
        return torch.cos(2 * pi * (t[..., None] * self.w + self.b))
```

The [blocks\.py L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L7) class, located in [`src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py), generates Fourier features from an input tensor\. This technique maps the input data into a higher\-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions, which can help neural networks better capture complex relationships within the data\. The layer is initialized with a specified number of Fourier components\. It utilizes learnable parameters, [blocks\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L10) and [blocks\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L11), which are registered as buffers\. These buffers are part of the model's state and are saved and loaded with it but are not updated by optimizers during training\. The [blocks\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L20) method initializes [blocks\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L10) and [blocks\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L11) by sampling values from a normal distribution\. In its forward pass, the class computes [blocks\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L4), transforming the input tensor [Makefile L52](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/Makefile#L52) into its Fourier representation\. This process is a foundational building block for constructing various deep learning architectures within the Foundry framework\. For further details on other common neural network components, refer to [Neural Network Building Blocks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#neural-network-building-blocks)\.### Broadcastable Dropout Layer

```
class Dropout(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, broadcast_dim: int | None = None, p_drop: float = 0.15) -> None:
        super(Dropout, self).__init__()
        # Sampler for generating dropout mask
        self.sampler = torch.distributions.bernoulli.Bernoulli(
            torch.tensor([1 - p_drop])
        )
        self.broadcast_dim = broadcast_dim
        self.p_drop = p_drop

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if not self.training:
            return x

        shape = list(x.shape)
        if self.broadcast_dim is not None:
            # If broadcast_dim is set, apply dropout along that dimension
            shape[self.broadcast_dim] = 1
        
        # Generate mask: 1s with probability (1 - p_drop), 0s with p_drop
        mask = self.sampler.sample(shape).to(x.device).view(shape)

        # Apply mask and scale output
        x = mask * x / (1.0 - self.p_drop)
        return x
```

The [blocks\.py L32](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L32) class in [`src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py) implements a specialized dropout mechanism, designed to improve the generalization of neural networks by randomly setting a fraction of input units to zero during training\. This particular implementation offers an optional feature: broadcasting the dropout mask across a specified dimension\. This means that instead of dropping individual elements independently, entire rows or columns of a tensor can be zeroed out along a chosen dimension, which can be beneficial in certain architectural contexts\. During the training phase, the mechanism utilizes a [blocks\.py L37](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/model/layers/blocks.py#L37) distribution to generate the necessary binary mask\. This mask is then applied to the input, and the remaining active elements are scaled to maintain the expected sum of activations, a standard practice in dropout to ensure consistent output magnitudes between training and inference\.## Model Training Harness

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundry employs a robust training harness built upon PyTorch Lightning Fabric to manage the entire lifecycle of deep learning models, from initial training and validation to checkpointing\. This system supports advanced training methodologies crucial for developing sophisticated biomolecular models, including distributed training, mixed precision computing, gradient accumulation, and Exponential Moving Average \(EMA\)\.

 The core of this harness is a flexible trainer designed to orchestrate the training process\. It handles the setup of the underlying Fabric instance, configuring accelerators, distributed training strategies, and precision settings\. This design ensures models can be efficiently trained across various hardware environments, including specialized Intel XPU devices\.

 The training harness also provides comprehensive state management, allowing for the saving and loading of model, optimizer, and scheduler states\. This capability is essential for resuming training from a specific point or for deploying pre\-trained models\. Gradient management features, such as gradient clipping and mechanisms to skip updates for non\-finite gradients, further enhance training stability\. Additionally, the system integrates with Hydra for declarative configuration, promoting modularity and reproducibility in model, optimizer, and scheduler construction\. The architecture also allows for external components to interact with the training process through a flexible callback system, described in [Extensible Callback System](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#extensible-callback-system)\.### Core FabricTrainer Architecture and Training Lifecycle

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) serves as an abstract base class that orchestrates the entire deep learning training process within Foundry\. It is designed to provide a standardized, yet flexible, framework for model training, validation, and state management\. The trainer manages the training lifecycle from its initialization and setup using [fabric\.py L163](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L163) to the execution of training and validation loops\.

 The core responsibility of [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) is to provide a consistent structure for managing epochs, data loading, validation scheduling, and checkpointing\. While it handles the overarching training process through its [fabric\.py L329](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L329) method, it defines abstract methods, [fabric\.py L661](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L661) and [fabric\.py L681](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L681), which subclasses must implement\. These abstract methods require model\-specific logic for the forward and backward passes during training and the forward pass during validation\. This design ensures that the trainer can be specialized for different model architectures while maintaining a common set of training functionalities\.

 The trainer's lifecycle begins with its initialization, where it configures the underlying PyTorch Lightning Fabric instance\. This setup involves defining parameters such as accelerators, distributed training strategies, precision settings, callbacks, and loggers\. The [fabric\.py L329](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L329) method then acts as the primary entry point for initiating training\. It orchestrates the overall training process, including data loader setup, model, optimizer, and scheduler initialization, and handling the loading or resumption from checkpoints\. Within the [fabric\.py L329](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L329) method, the trainer calls [fabric\.py L510](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L510) to execute a single training epoch, which involves processing batches, accumulating gradients, and updating optimizer states\. Similarly, the [fabric\.py L598](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L598) executes a single validation epoch, where the model's performance is evaluated without computing gradients\. For more details on the advanced training features and state management within [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56), refer to [Advanced Training Techniques and State Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness-advanced-training-techniques-and-state-management)\. The integration of [fabric\.py L163](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L163) also enables scalable training across various hardware and distributed strategies, as elaborated in [Distributed Training and Hardware Acceleration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness-distributed-training-and-hardware-acceleration)\.### Advanced Training Techniques and State Management

```
class MyTrainer(FabricTrainer):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        # Configure gradient clipping in the constructor
        self.clip_grad_max_norm = 1.0  # Example value

    def training_step(self, batch: Any, batch_idx: int, is_accumulating: bool) -> None:
        # Example training step
        output = self.state["model"](batch)
        loss = output.mean()
        self.fabric.backward(loss)
        self._current_train_return = {"loss": loss}

        if not is_accumulating:
            # step_optimizer is called internally by train_loop
            # after gradient accumulation steps are met.
            # It handles gradient clipping, optimizer step, and EMA updates.
            pass # `step_optimizer` is called automatically by the `train_loop`

    def validation_step(self, batch: Any, batch_idx: int, val_loader_name: str | None = None) -> dict:
        # Stub for validation step
        return {}

# --- Usage Example ---
trainer = MyTrainer(
    output_dir="my_checkpoints",
    # ... other trainer configurations
)
# trainer.fit(...) # Would call training_step, which then uses step_optimizer

# Manual checkpoint saving (also called automatically by fit())
trainer.save_checkpoint()

# Manual checkpoint loading
latest_ckpt_path = trainer.get_latest_checkpoint(Path("my_checkpoints/ckpt"))
if latest_ckpt_path:
    trainer.load_checkpoint(latest_ckpt_path)
```

The [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) facilitates robust and efficient deep learning training through several advanced techniques\. It supports gradient clipping via the [train\.py L31](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L31) configuration, which helps prevent exploding gradients during optimization\. To maintain training stability, the system can skip optimizer updates when non\-finite gradients are detected, a safeguard against numerical instability\. These gradient management operations are centralized within the [fabric\.py L730](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L730) method\.

 Comprehensive state management is another core capability, allowing for the reliable saving and loading of model, optimizer, and scheduler states through [fabric\.py L815](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L815) and [fabric\.py L868](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L868)\. This supports training resumption and model deployment\. The checkpointing mechanism also provides flexible weight loading options and the ability to freeze specific parameters, enabling scenarios such as fine\-tuning pre\-trained models or training only a subset of a model's layers\. For further details on the overarching training harness, refer to [Model Training Harness](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/foundry#model-training-harness)\.### Distributed Training and Hardware Acceleration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [fabric\.py L56](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) orchestrates scalable training across diverse hardware configurations, leveraging PyTorch Lightning Fabric\. This includes support for multi\-GPU and multi\-node training through the [fabric\.py L22](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L22), which handles the complexities of distributed data parallel processing\. For specialized hardware, Foundry integrates support for Intel XPU devices using a custom [xpu\_accelerator\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/xpu_accelerator.py#L9) and [single\_xpu\_strategy\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/xpu/single_xpu_strategy.py#L13)\. This allows for efficient training and inference on Intel hardware, including mixed precision operations\. To manage output in these distributed environments, [ddp\.py L58](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/blob/551a90103a51d0bff27e269fe454fdba4aefb274/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L58) ensures that logging information is consolidated and originates only from the primary process, preventing redundant logs and simplifying debugging across multiple computational nodes or devices\. The overall architecture is designed to manage the training state, including the model, optimizer, and scheduler, and supports robust checkpointing for saving and loading progress across distributed runs\.
